Just in time to seek justice for the Ye family's girl!

That's the reasoning. I was still worried about not having an excuse to seek justice for my Master Uncle, but now that my martial arts have improved, and with the help of the Cang Song swordsman, if the Diancang Sect wants to fight, then we can set out on an expedition to Dali another day.

That's precisely how it should be. That Diancang faction used to provoke during the conflict with Jileiao Sect, taking advantage of our heavy losses at that time. After defeating one of our seniors, they have always considered themselves the victors and have held a high stance within the sect ever since, behaving condescendingly in Sichuan. I've never liked them.
Even if they don't come, I still want to find the time to go to Dali and beat them up. Isn't that just perfect?
It seems there's nothing much to say. Aren't they just a bunch of crazy people?
Aren't we supposed to talk about the Diancang Sect? Go ahead and say it, Senior Brother.
Policy towards the Diancang Sect
Elder Brother, what are you doing...?
No matter what secrets the Ye siblings are hiding, it doesn't matter. In any case, if it can make the Diancang Sect unhappy, why not go for it?
I was just saying it; did you really take it seriously? If I actually went to discuss it, I'm afraid I wouldn't even finish a sentence before her brother would kill me with a single sword strike.
Unfortunately, my heart belongs to someone else. Otherwise, could you help me discuss the possibility of marrying as a primary wife or a concubine?

No need, thank you. Although Sister Yunshang is as beautiful as a flower, unfortunately, my body is weak and truly cannot withstand her antics. If I were to marry her, it would not only be a case of fresh flowers being inserted into cow dung, but rather a mutual waste.
...Senior Brother is going to marry Yunshang?
Sure, why don't you take action?
Huh?

Third Senior Brother, don't speak sarcastically! She only acts cute in front of you, and even knows how to hold back when teasing you; that's just her flattering you! Where is she still a child? She's at the age where she can get married. I really want to play matchmaker and connect her with a junior brother!
Aren't these just her childish antics, playing and causing a ruckus? Why are you taking her so seriously?

She even took advantage of me while I was bathing to steal my clothes, using a branch to dangle them and extort me! When I refused to agree, she really threw my clothes off the cliff and went to knock on the female disciple's door to gather to watch me!
That little brat put firecrackers in my chest, causing them to explode behind me while I was walking. I wasn't hurt, but I was so scared that I nearly lost control!
Fourth Senior Brother, why do you hold such deep resentment towards others?

The illness has been treated to a satisfactory extent; whether one lives or dies, it is time to know when to go home. Why are they still lingering? Now even the attending doctor has left, yet they are still living comfortably. We must not be deceived by treacherous individuals, better to stand in front of the blade for others.
Third Senior Brother, you are too soft‑hearted. Those siblings are hiding some enormous secret, and it's very mysterious.

Although it is a matter of another sect, the Ye siblings have a pitiable background, and I feel a deep sympathy for them. How can I bear to stand by and do nothing while they are in danger, especially since they are seeking refuge in our sect?
Let's talk about the Diancang Sect. This time they are causing a stir, and it goes without saying that it must be related to the matters concerning the Ye siblings, right?
Policy towards the Diancang Sect
—That's assuming our sect can keep its footing steady. If we suffer any more losses, the Beggar Sect will immediately beat the drowning dog. Do you believe it?

If that's the case, then there's no need to worry about them. You've already driven back the traitors. Given the Beggar Sect's despicable nature, they'll put on a show of bluster, then gradually calm down and pretend nothing happened. The next time you cross paths, they'll shift the blame to the New Faction, claiming it was the New Faction that attacked our sect, and so on.
...Th-That makes sense. Buy low—it couldn't be cheaper.

Besides, those Beggar Sect elders didn't choose to be beggars willingly. If there's a chance to get rich, of course they wouldn't miss it. If I were Uncle Shangguan, why would I waste my effort trying to win over anyone else? I'd take advantage of the Beggar Sect's fall from power to seduce and recruit them.

The Shangguan Family conspired with the Songshan Fujian Branch to support that traitor Uncle Tang Shouhong in trying to seize power, right? This shows that the Shangguan Family's supposed 'washing their hands in a golden basin' was just a pretense. In reality, they have ulterior motives toward our Tang Clan.
You shouldn't say that. How did the Shangguan Family get dragged into this?
Who knows, the mastermind behind this might even be the Shangguan Family.
Please, they are beggars; what do you expect them to know? Whatever the leading beggar says, that's how it will be done.
I was wondering if that might be the case... but that's just too thoughtless.

As for the Beggar Sect, the Old Faction is in control now, right? They're eager to make achievements and restore their reputation. They're probably trying to take advantage of the chaos in the Jianghu—striking blindly while the other sects are too busy to defend themselves.
Policy towards the Beggar Sect
Sigh, fine. Let's set this matter aside for now. What I fear is that the Sect Leader may not have a few more years to wait.
Third Junior Brother, you hear that? This girl clearly hasn't awakened to such things yet. Why not wait a few more years?
Not interested.
What do you mean 'not bad'? You're not very interested in any of them, or you think each one is pretty good?
Not bad
Uh... uh...
Oh, not bad. Is there anyone among them that catches your eye?
I think so.
Hmph
Alright, Junior Brother, calm down. Step back a bit and give them some space to talk.
Those guys all had ulterior motives. Not a single one of them was any good. Of course I have to protect Little Junior Sister!
Zhao Huo, what's wrong with you?!
Yes, they were all chased away by Senior Brother.
When Elder Nangong previously advocated for studying abroad, were there not any young heroes who admired your beauty and came to get close to you?
You don't know the Heaven and Earth Silent Power, but I do. So I'm smarter, and you're the silly one.
That's not what I meant, you late‑blooming silly girl.
And you too, Senior Brother.
Of course. Father, Mother, you, Second Senior Brother, Third Senior Brother. Everyone.
I'm not asking if you'll obey. I'm asking if you want to. This is a question that affects your whole life. Isn't there anyone you've ever cared about in your heart?
...Nothing. I will follow Father's arrangements.
Master wants to arrange for you and me to marry, to become husband and wife. How do you feel about that?
You want to run wildly and roar, to escape this place, but your feet feel as if they are filled with lead, unable to move an inch.
Ah, if I were not afraid of death, why would I have lived to this day? I have long known that today would eventually come; this is a good thing, this is a good thing.
Hmm
Alright, Little Junior Sister, come here. Eldest Senior Brother wants to ask you something.
...With the Sect Leader being this way now, can you really bear to leave the Little Junior Sister helpless and alone?
Isn't it because we grew up together since we were little? She's like a real little sister to me. How could I make a move on her... Just thinking about it gives me chills, alright?

Eldest Senior Brother,, Little Junior Sister has also grown up under your watch. Everyone cherishes her like a precious gem, afraid she might break. Why do you not show her any affection? Instead, every time you hear her name, you seem to want to run away.
Little Junior Sister, please come over here
No, there probably isn't a chance
I actually stopped them. If Senior Martial Brother were not around, the Little Junior Sister would have no one to rely on. Perhaps I would have had a chance... perhaps I would have had a chance...
I almost fell for Eldest Senior Brother's trick again. Good thing I have you, Junior Brother.
Stay put, you little bastard.
Gwaah~ Junior Brother, y-you actually betrayed me!
What?!
Hey! Second Junior Brother! You dare show your face back here?!
No way~ Third Junior Brother, you're being too suspicious. Human nature is inherently good—have you forgotten?
It's probably just me being overly sensitive, but let me say this upfront: don't even think about running away.
Eldest Senior Brother, when the Sect Leader was awake, besides discussing the future of our sect, he also entrusted me with another important matter—handling Little Junior Sister's future marriage.
Master's Instructions (Regarding the Future of Little Junior Sister)
I know that.
Eldest Senior Brother, as the chief disciple of our sect, you must be more serious from now on. The rise and fall of our sect are closely tied to you.
Third Senior Brother, this is clearly a sign of distrust.
...What's past is past. There's no use dwelling on it.
Forget it, believe it or not, I've made myself clear anyway.
Sigh. The moral standards of this age are declining.
Hahaha, that's funny. Junior Brother, you really are obscene.
Hahaha!
Hahaha!
a good stabbing of the lady.
But rather with—
Little Junior Sister, quickly cover your ears!
What I'm afraid of is that the word 'assassination' really was an assassination—just not one done with a knife.

On the Flower List, first place is the Female Top Scholar, second is the Female Runner-Up, third is the Female Second Runner-Up. Then come the Provincial Scholar and the Bachelor. At the very bottom is the Grand Historian.
Another time you said you were going to assassinate the Grand Historian. And guess what? You were in a brothel.
The one who invited me for drinks was the courtesan. And a courtesan is also called a 'female top scholar.' How come you didn't know that?
You think we believe you? Back in the day, you'd disappear and lie, saying the top scholar invited you for drinks. And guess what? You were in a brothel.
...That's too absurd.
I originally wanted to turn the horse around and take down Wanyan Xun as well. But as expected, I couldn't do it; I almost lost my life. So, I went back home.
Hahaha!
How can you be like that? He'd already surrendered, and you still took him out? Hahahaha!

That bastard saw the banner in my hand and turned pale as ash, not daring to resist. He shouted: 'I am innocent! Your Majesty, please investigate!' I rode over, chopped off his head with one swing, then spun around and used it as a hidden weapon to kill another pursuer.

I roared at him: 'You traitor, Pusan Anzhen! How dare you collude with mountain bandits to ambush the Emperor! All soldiers, charge! Capture the traitor Pusan Anzhen! Anyone who disobeys or resists arrest shall be executed without mercy!'
Oh, at that time I seized Wanyan Xun's banner. I pretended to be one of Wanyan Xun's envoys and charged my horse toward Pusan Anzhen, who was coming out of the camp to greet me.
Stop. Why are you swaying back and forth? That's not how you ride a horse!
As a result, a large crowd of people arrived. I had a sudden idea, stole the horses from the dog emperor's personal guards and led them on a chase.
That's what I shouted.
A once-in-a-lifetime chance to leave your name in history! Whoever wants to follow me, Tang, to take the Dog Emperor's head—come on!
It was said that the Jin Emperor, Wanyan Xun, had received a letter from someone and was going to personally visit the Xiangyang front lines to comfort Jin Marshal Pusan Anzhen.
It turns out that the one leading them, Wan Sheng of the Golden Blade, had gotten some news.
Mountain Bandit King... Good heavens... How did the Tang Clan end up with such an unworthy descendant as you?
Beat them into submission and become the Mountain Bandit King.
That's why I had to—
That's true! But they've claimed their mountains and made themselves kings. Why would they listen to your commands?

It's not sudden at all. Think about it—mountain bandits are everywhere. In Song territory, they're rebels. In the Jin Kingdom, they're 'green forest' heroes who oppose the court. Aren't they just ready-made anti-Jin heroes?
What's going on?! This is so sudden!
Then I went to a joint oath-taking rally of mountain bandits from Yingtian, Kaifeng, Henan, and Hezhong. Fight their mother!

What about it? I have to care about the beautiful rivers and mountains seized by the Jin, and how the common people are living there. Since I'm going to care, naturally I start with the brothels. Those women are the most pitiable among the pitiable.
You still have the leisure to visit brothels...?
Genius Fang Liang, I went out of the city afterwards. Then, I headed north and wandered through the Jin Kingdom, stopping by a few Pleasure Houses along the way.

That night, Danxiazi, Old General Zhao Fang, the commander of Xiangyang, and the soldiers drank to their heart's content all night long. We drank so much that we finished all the wine at the tavern in Xiangyang.

After that, I assisted the soldiers of Xiangyang, freely engaging in guerrilla tactics and causing chaos. When there was nothing else to do, I would run and let others chase me. Whenever I spotted someone who looked like a hundred‑man commander or a thousand‑man commander, I would go over and take their head. It was exhilarating to see the invading Jin soldiers flee in panic.
Because your Eldest Senior Brother has graced them with his magnificent presence!
But this kind of balance was about to collapse.
Under his command, the Song soldiers could just barely contend with the Jin people's cavalry.
There, I encountered the legendary Daoist General Danxiazi. To be fair, although his title of General is somewhat honorary, the soldiers truly obey him without question.
I first went to the battlefield of the Song‑Jin War. The scale of that battle made the Battle of Jiangling seem like child's play.
Alright, everyone move back a bit. I'm about to tell a story!
The moment I announced the title, they all got that look on their faces.
I haven't even started talking yet, so why are you all looking at me with such suspicious eyes?
Oh, that's great! I was afraid you wouldn't ask. I went to the Jin Kingdom.
Flying Hero's Journey of a Thousand Miles
Fortunately, I'm not the only one who believes in Second Senior Brother.

I'll go find him myself. Just rest assured. Ever since we were young, whenever he made a mistake or suffered some grievance and hid away crying, which time was it not me who found him? This time will be no exception. Leave it to me.
Let's assume that's true for now. But when we encounter Second Junior Brother, we still can't go for the kill. Don't forget that the Sect Leader's life and death are in someone else's hands.
Well... He only did it to make us fearful, to use it as leverage. What good intentions could there be in that?
Conversely, if the master did not take the Corpse Heart Pill, wouldn't he have ascended to immortality long ago?
Exactly. This traitor who betrayed his master and destroyed his ancestors cannot be let off easily.

Hmm... According to what you've said, Master was hanging by a thread at the time, and that's when Second Junior Brother seized the opportunity, forced him to take the Supreme Bliss Sect's Corpse Heart Pill, and from then on he's been stiff as a corpse, sleeping without waking. Is that right?
I'm talking about the traitor, Tang Zheng.
Are you talking about Uncle Tang Shouhong?
What does Eldest Senior Brother think about the matter of our sect's traitor?
Of course, just wait and see. I have my own clever plans‑watch me take a trip to Woyun Ridge and handle things efficiently and decisively.
Really?
As for the matter with the Flying Stone Gang, to put it simply, I have a way to turn enemies into friends without shedding blood.
There's no need for you to worry about this; from this moment on, everything will gradually improve.
Situation of our sect
Leave the seat
Alright, everyone stop joking around and take your seats. We still have important matters to discuss.
No, go to the side
Okay
Where would I get breasts from! Don't talk nonsense, you scoundrel!
That's right. After all, Little Junior Sister was raised on your breast milk.
Is... is that so?
Not surprising, really. After all, if there's anyone who dotes on Little Junior Sister the most, it's him.
Little Junior Sister, why are you...?
Excuse me.
Okay.
Little Junior Sister, can you stick to someone else? You're about to tear my clothes apart.
As for my heart, let it be severed from today onward.
That's good. Now that Eldest Senior Brother is back, Little Junior Sister's future is taken care of.
Ah, Little Junior Sister is pressed up against Eldest Senior Brother, her little hand clutching his sleeve and refusing to let go.
I've returned from visiting Master.
Okay.
Indeed, Eldest Senior Brother, go check on the Sect Leader. Little Junior Sister is also upstairs.
Ha, you go prepare the wine, I have a good story to tell. These things are not urgent; we can talk about them later.
Huh?
Eldest Senior Brother went to the Jin Kingdom. He said he was going to assassinate the Jin Emperor.
Where exactly did he go?
Eldest Senior Brother told me not to tell. He said if I did, it might expose his whereabouts.
Junior Brother, so you knew where Eldest Senior Brother was all along. Why didn't you say anything?
Ha, it's a long story. You can ask Zhao Huo first.  I'll go have a drink to wet my throat, then I'll tell you slowly. I'm going to visit Master first.
But Eldest Senior Brother, you've been missing all this time. Where exactly did you go?

And Eldest Senior Brother says he's not cut out to be Sect Leader. With just that one shout, didn't all the senior brothers get their fighting spirits roused? No wonder the Sect Leader favors Eldest Senior Brother.
Back when the Supreme Bliss Sect rose from Western Xia, we didn't come out unscathed either.
It truly isn't worth it; it's like a minor sorcerer facing a great sorcerer.
Indeed. Flesh and blood will eventually decay. Bones can be dug up and ground to dust. But our will shall not bend.
‑Even if we die in battle, we won't die alone. We'll have our own family with us.

That's right. The Outer Fort was built precisely to resist armies. We dare to go against even the old emperor himself. I ask you—in the Central Plains Wulin, whose guts are bigger than the Tang Clan's? Amidst the storms of the Jianghu, what is there that should make the Tang family's children tremble in fear?
Fight their mother!

Tell me, when Emperor Xuanzong of the previous dynasty was forced by An Lushan to take refuge in Shu, yet still wanted to throw his weight around, impose heavy taxes, and force the people to risk their lives building him a new palace—what did our Tang ancestors say about that?

Those who toy with others will be toyed with in return. So just don't bully people! If you don't want your own mother dragged into it, you'd better behave yourself. The law may not reach you, but human decency and reason do. The scales are in people's hearts.

That's right! It's 'Fight your mother!' When we see someone bullying others on the road, we help bully them back. When we run into someone who absolutely won't repent, we'll go after his mother if we have to.
What kind of principle is that?
The correct answer is 'Fight your mother.'
Hahaha, Fourth Junior Brother, you really have no conscience! Whew~
See injustice on the road' — does that mean I get a share of the spoils?
Junior Brother, why did you suddenly curse?
Fuck your mother?
Not quite, it's not that grand; be more straightforward.
Chivalrous and righteous?
Three junior brothers, let me test you. In the Tang Clan's way, when we see injustice on the road, what is our principle?
This won't do. Negotiation is fine, but your overly cautious demeanor is rather embarrassing for the Tang Clan.

Eldest Senior Brother, the Jianghu is currently facing a tumultuous time, with various sects on high alert. What strategies do you have in mind? It would be wise to share them so that everyone can discuss and consider them together, rather than acting rashly.
It's still up to you to handle the internal matters; I'll take care of those external issues.
Damn it all!
Your life is worthless, hahahaha!
Why me? There are so many senior and junior brothers in our sect; why does it have to be me?
Of course it's you.
Why are you all looking at me? Are you referring to me when you say 'Junior Brother'?
Keeping things steady inside still requires you. As for those outside matters, Junior Brother and I can handle them, right??
That is indeed the case...

To resolve these matters in our sect, what we lack is not decision‑makers, but executors. If I became Sect Leader, I definitely wouldn't be better than you. On the other hand, there are things I can get done out there that you might not be able to.
Why?!
No, Third Junior Brother. You should hold on a while longer.
Isn't that right? Now that you're back to take charge, Eldest Senior Brother, it's wonderful! I, the Acting Sect Leader, can finally step down with honor.
Hmm... I understand the situation now. So many things happened while I was away.
Oh, I'm back!
Senior Brother!!
For example, fuck your ances—
Like what?
I imagined the future a little, and all the harsh words I wanted to say to Eldest Senior Brother sprouted up like bamboo shoots after the rain.
If you're doing crosstalk, just do crosstalk. Why does your face look so fierce?
If Senior Brother were to appear right now, I would consider retiring to perform crosstalk!
Once the Tang Clan gets through this crisis, I'll retire and do crosstalk.
Something so trivial and natural—you don't need to give up your dream for it. I'll make it happen anyway.
Junior Brother...!
It is indeed my long‑held wish, but my current wish is for the safety of our sect.
Are you serious? Isn't this your long‑held wish?
...If Eldest Senior Brother returns, I would be willing to never become an inner disciple.
I will no longer make a fuss about wanting to become an inner disciple.
Huh...? But I don't have those kinds of feelings for Little Junior Sister.
That kind of thing is impossible, so you don't need to worry about it.
That said, if Little Junior Sister comes to me herself, I'll still give it serious thought.
Stop pretending. I've known all along that you, you beast, have already fallen for someone else.
...What a tremendous determination that must be.
I will no longer compete with Senior Martial Brother for Little Junior Sister!
I will no longer compete with Senior Martial Brother for Little Junior Sister.
I, Tang Weiyuan, also swear: I will never again try to collect the drinking money Eldest Senior Brother owes me.

Sigh! Hard, truly hard. Eldest Senior Brother, oh Eldest Senior Brother~ Do me a favor and come back to the mountain soon. If you don't return, the Tang Clan will be ruined by my hands. I, Tang Sheng, swear to the heavens: if Eldest Senior Brother returns safely, I will never force him to study or practice calligraphy again.

In the Jianghu, I always treat others with courtesy, but they may not have good intentions. I want to repay wrongdoing with virtue, but in the end I get taken advantage of like soft soil being dug deep. I can keep the peace, but it would mean dragging my fellow disciples down with me—they'll be looked down upon and beaten or killed at will.

So that's how it is? The things Eldest Senior Brother has done are certainly not what a gentleman should do. However, if it weren't for this, our sect might have been trampled long before it had a chance to revive.

In that case, it's possible that Senior Brother truly has foresight. If he hadn't invited Lady Shi away, making the Flying Stone Gang hesitate for fear of harming her, how could both sides have fought so fiercely until now, only determining victory and defeat without deciding life or death?
Junior Brother, with such ruthlessness, aren't you afraid of losing your virtue?
With a heartless, Heaven-defying dog like you in our sect, no wonder Eldest Senior Brother had to hide her away.
Otherwise, even if we don't use her to threaten the Flying Stone Gang, we should still torture her and kill her as a show of force.
It's just a pity that we don't know where Senior Brother has hidden that gang leader's wife.
That's right, and the battle of Jiangling would have been a perfect opportunity to attack our sect too.
So if Eldest Senior Brother hadn't kidnapped the gang leader's wife and made them hesitant, the Flying Stone Gang would have likely taken advantage of our sect's earlier decline and struck to kill.
That's actually true.

On the contrary, our sect has never feared the words of others; saying we are both righteous and wicked is not an exaggeration. Though we're one of the Three Great Families, quite a few have dared to challenge us over the years. So wouldn't we be the perfect target?

Think about it, the Flying Stone Gang wants to learn from the Beggar Sect to establish a reputation and become a top gang in the Wulin. Strength, connections, and reputation are all essential; they wouldn't have time to curry favor with the six major sects, so how could they afford to make enemies for no reason?
The six major sects are closely connected. Qingcheng and Emei are among them. If they are attacked, how can the other four sects stand by and do nothing?
Junior Brother... is your mind really that simple? It's surprising given how complex your features are.
Why? The Shu region isn't just the Tang Clan. Why doesn't the Flying Stone Gang go pick a fight with Emei or Qingcheng?
Why don't they go attack Qingcheng and Emei?
Well, I hate to admit it, but you're right.
Third Senior Brother, Junior Brother pronounced that 'fight their mother' perfectly. He sounds more like a Tang Clan disciple than you do.

It's hard to say whether the other sects fear us. In any case, Tang Clan isn't afraid of them. It's best if our waters don't mix with theirs. If they have to bully people, then we'll fight their mother.
Oh, I rhymed, I really have talent.
It's better if they're truly afraid. Then they won't come bothering us all day.
Junior Brother may be unpleasant to look at, but occasionally he says something very learned. The only person in our sect who can persuade Third Senior Brother in just a few words is him.
...Junior Brother is right. The Tang Clan is just a household with the surname Tang, living in Shu. Why should we form factions?

Generally speaking, gentlemen form friendships with gentlemen based on shared principles; petty people form friendships with petty people based on shared gain. That's only natural. We're not strange or difficult—why wouldn't we make friends? I just mean we don't need to form factions.
Makes sense.
Stop, stop‑both of you, don't get off topic. It's important to discuss the matter at hand.
Junior Brother may be ugly and unpleasant, but occasionally he says something astonishing. The only person in our sect who can debate with Third Senior Brother is him.

This statement is incorrect. A gentleman upholds righteousness, acts with loyalty and trustworthiness, and values their reputation. By cultivating himself and serving the country this way, he benefits others who share his principles and works together with a united heart—that is the fellowship of gentlemen. The Six Major Sects stand guard over the Central Plains, keeping evil spirits and petty villains from running wild.

Normally there's nothing urgent, yet they gather together, calling themselves the Six Major Sects, acting as if they have the final say in all matters of the Wulin. To put it bluntly, isn't it just for the sake of reputation? I have no respect for such false friends.

What's wrong with that? What petty people love are salaries and benefits. What they covet are wealth and goods. When their interests align, they temporarily band together as friends—but it's all false.
If you say it like that, then this clan's style is both righteous and wicked, not aligning with any factions. It's no wonder that both the righteous and the wicked fear the Tang Clan.
That's right. Those who can't become friends will become enemies sooner or later. We might as well strike first. It's just a pity we missed our chance.

Do you not see the struggles of Jianghu throughout history? From where does the chaos in the country arise? The Flying Stone Gang has established itself in Shu, and one mountain cannot accommodate two tigers; what is destined to come will eventually arrive.
I think so too

Junior Brother, you're wrong about this. Do you really think that if Eldest Senior Brother hadn't kidnapped someone's wife, everything would be fine? The Flying Stone Gang is ambitious. Sooner or later, they'll have to fight it out with our sect.
...Forget it.
Isn't it considered a deep grudge to take someone else's spouse away?
One shouldn't say it like that; harmony is of utmost importance in all matters. Since there are no deep grudges or enmities, it's better to avoid fighting if possible.

The Flying Stone Gang was originally just a minor, insignificant faction. However, with the decline of the Beggar Sect following the Jiangling incident, they seized the opportunity to rise. Yet, their members are a mixed bag, and they may not necessarily be our match.

It's too late. All my ambitions, all my hopes of clearing out the ruler's corrupt advisors and bringing peace to the nation—what a waste. Little did I know that the first half of my life was spent studying under the cold light of a lamp, while the second half has been consumed by endless paperwork at my desk. My precious youth has long been wasted! In the midst of mediocrity, I suddenly look back and find my hair has turned white on both sides. Alas.
Acting Sect Leader, you shouldn't worry so much, or you'll age quickly.
Understood
If the news spreads, the fact that the sect leader has fallen ill will inevitably become known to everyone. With the mast fallen and the oars broken, this ship will sink regardless of our efforts.

No matter what, I ask you two junior brothers to stay vigilant. Continue to investigate Eldest Senior Brother's whereabouts, but keep it quiet. As for Second Senior Brother—regarding the traitor Tang Zheng of our sect—hold off on that for now.
With Eldest Senior Brother's fear-nothing-in-heaven-or-earth nature, how could he be afraid to fight? Although he often disappears without a trace, this time feels a bit unusual.
...Eldest Senior Brother went to the Jin Kingdom and has yet to return. The Sect Leader intends to keep the disciples from knowing, so I should continue to keep it a secret.
That's only natural. After all, his wife is missing. It's not as if a few words of surrender or an apology will make her pop back into existence.
Even if I'm willing to make peace, the other side shows no appreciation for the gesture.

This third challenge letter is written in harsh, angry language. It says that if the eldest senior brother continues to play the turtle hiding in its shell... if he doesn't show up for the duel, he will lead his men to attack the Tang Clan and fight to the death.
Unfortunately, Eldest Senior Brother has taken away someone's wife, and her whereabouts remain unknown to this day. GGang Leader Shi is not someone who will let this go just by saving face.

You can't really blame him. In normal martial world duels, if one party doesn't show up, the referee will declare that opponent a coward who lost without fighting. Spread that around, and it's even more shameful than actually losing.
How can I not be anxious? This is no ordinary situation, sigh. This is the third letter urging a duel that the Flying Stone Gang leader has sent.
Yes, it has always been like this.
Yes. However, in my opinion, there's no need for us to be so anxious. When the time comes, Eldest Senior Brother will naturally make his appearance.
...Is there still no news of Eldest Senior Brother?

Upon hearing that the leader was gravely ill, Lu Weng felt a surge of emotions and generously opened their purse, clearing the old debt from the previous generation of the Tang Clan that had been borrowed to buy rice and alleviate the hardships of the famine year.

Long Xiang left without hesitation; the figure in white vanished. The wind blew, and even a wisp of her lingering fragrance was gone, as if she had never come.
I'm leaving. One last piece of advice: I hope you'll take care of yourself and cherish the people around you. Don't let her‑who chose you out of everyone‑end up heartbroken and miserable.
Sigh, I'm not expecting you to repay me.
...Thank you for looking after me all this time, Hero Zhao. If you ever run into trouble in the future, I, Long, will certainly repay you.
You... take care.
You should go
...well, as for that...
Do you have to be so heartless!

You already have those feelings for me; from now on we can no longer be siblings. You have only two choices: either let me leave the mountain, or I will jump off the cliff. I can't defeat you, and it won't be so easy for you to stop me from ending my life.
......If you hadn't said anything, we could've stayed good friends.
Sigh... I knew I couldn't persuade you. So, shall we go back to being friends?
I can't beat you. Marry as many as you like, but I will never be counted among your wives and concubines.
That's going too far‑having three wives and four concubines has never been uncommon in our dynasty, has it?

...My master once said that faithless, fickle people lack integrity and are exactly the sort you must not befriend. If you can betray the one you love, sooner or later you'll betray friends and family as well.
Now it's time to calm down, right?
...I can't beat you.

Her words were cold, but the sword she wielded retained a lingering warmth. The soft blade coiled around her fingers and ripped you open; at first glance the wounds were shocking‑enough to have you die ten times over‑yet none of them struck a vital point. Each was a marvel down to the tiniest stroke: a shallow nick, a gentle slice. You were rendered unable to fight not by your body, but because your heart was broken.
Sister Xiang...
I'm leaving. I hope you'll take care of yourself and cherish the people around you. Don't let her‑who chose you out of so many‑end up heartbroken and miserable.
But because you harbor those feelings for me, from now on we can no longer be sister and brother. Today I'm not cutting you off‑I am severing the bond between us.

...By palace rules, one cannot show mercy to the faithless and fickle. But I owe you too much ‑ taking your life would be unjustifiable, and it would weigh on my conscience. If you hadn't spoken up, we could have remained good friends.
Uh!
Oh, so this is what you wanted to say.
I was thinking, if you don't have anywhere else to go, why not come with us so we can look out for one another? We can take our time deciding what to do for a living later.
So what were you originally going to say, and why did you suddenly freeze?
...Sister Xiang, the Tang Clan hasn't disbanded yet ‑ where would an enemy come from? Calm down.
Who goes there! Don't harm my brother!
Were you struck at an acupoint by some kind of invisible Hidden Weapon?
To have met her and call each other brother and sister is already my good fortune; if I grow greedy and never content, even this hard‑won friendship will vanish.
What's wrong? Why aren't you talking anymore?

Perhaps I should be content. She is a peerless person ‑ a dragon among people ‑ and only because such a dragon was forced into shallow waters did she cross my path. She doesn't have to be with anyone; if she were to have a chivalrous companion, it should be a dashing hero like the Eldest Senior Brother, not someone like me.
What if?
Sister Xiang, what if... what if...
Hidden Deep in the Heart (Give Up)
Uh, you've hit the nail on the head ‑ I don't know how much time it'll take either.
Don't make it sound so easy. How long would that take? How would you even know where I went?
Don't worry. Once I've finished my business, I'll come find you myself.
I already owe you so much. To ask you to stay with me again and burden your life‑how could that be right? Don't make me feel even more guilty.
That's really going too far!

No‑ you finally made up your mind to retire from the Jianghu, didn't you? If a spiritless, stinky younger brother like you keeps hanging around me, you'll only drag down my sword and weaken my resolve.
...Why don't I keep you company?
I stubbornly stick to doing what's right; I'm the most reliable when it comes to keeping my word.
So stubborn
No, but I have to go ‑ I can't not go. The reason is probably about the same as why you've always stuck with the Tang Clan. Don't try to persuade me; I won't listen anyway.
Are you confident you can win?
Yes
Is that Shentu Long? Are you really planning to keep the appointment and face him?
When I'm really sulking, my face gets so sullen and ugly‑I don't want you to see it. So I'm leaving.

Because I still have unfinished business in the Jianghu: unsolved mysteries, unavenged grievances, and promises unmet. I am afraid too, but I also know that if I run away, the rest of my life will be melancholy and joyless.
Why... didn't you say you wanted to retire from the Wulin and never wield a sword again?
Let's put aside for now whether we'll be married; I'm willing to follow you into seclusion among the mountains and forests, but I cannot.
Ah...
It's not like that
So that means...?
Brother, you're wonderful ‑ you deserve anyone, even someone as insignificant as me.
What sort of person I am, I know myself‑I was never someone who could enter your favor. No need to spare my face; go ahead and refuse me without pity, just don't draw your sword.
Incredibly earnest
......Are you serious?

If I keep hiding my feelings, I'm afraid I'll regret it when I'm old and carry that regret for the rest of my life. Better to take the chance and say it outright‑hear you refuse me to my face‑and then I can finally put this to rest.

I know you care about my eldest senior brother. Even if we were reborn, there could be no comparing. Now that the Tang Clan has disbanded, we'll be going our separate ways, and I'm afraid we may never see each other again in this life.
I treat you like a younger brother ‑ I never expected you'd have such improper thoughts about me. Tsk tsk.
I‑Is it this early?
...What if I'm genuinely enamored with you? From the moment we first met, I had no good intentions.
W‑w‑well‑ you actually went to such lengths and sacrificed so much to look after someone as useless as me? Even if we're close, how could I possibly put you through this?

No. You already have a female confidante at your side, yet you still act so fickle. Even if the rites permit three wives and four concubines, Jinxiang Palace will not tolerate it. Your name will be written as the final entry on the Xi Hua Ling!
No need to be like that, right? If you don't agree, just pretend I never said anything.
Draw your blade. From this moment on, the bond between us as siblings is severed.
Miss Long, would you be willing to marry me and live with me? I will treat you well for the rest of my life; come rain or shine, I will continue to respect, love, and care for you as I do today.
What do you need to muster up the courage to tell me? Are you trying to challenge me?
...Sister Xiang, don't brush this off ‑ it took me so much courage to say it. You can refuse after you hear it, but at least let me finish before I lose my nerve.

Um... I, I originally wanted to repay your kindness, you know? But I just ended up causing you more and more trouble. At this rate, I'm afraid I won't be able to repay it even in my next life. Haha... how embarrassing.
So you actually minded?
I know you're being generous, but I do mind.
I don't mind

Little brother, I appreciate your kindness. But I can't keep clinging to you forever; sooner or later we'll have to part. So why not make up my mind now, give a wave and say goodbye‑clean and decisive.
You... if you have nowhere else to go, would you like to come with me?
Sister Xiang, would you like to come with me? (expressing their feelings)

Should I just quietly hide my feelings like this and take them to the grave? But if I speak them aloud, I'm afraid I'll be needlessly scorned by her. She‑she is probably infatuated with Senior Brother.
Sister Xiang, if you can't think of anywhere to go right now, how about going with me?
Hey... what's that expression? Are you thinking of something rude?

They haven't thought anything through; they are just being urged to leave, with nowhere to call home. I'm worried that their wallet will be stolen, leaving them penniless and squatting on the street, hugging their knees and crying. Ah... the more I think about it, the more uneasy I feel.

The Central Plains are so vast. If I leave the Tang Clan and Sister Xiang wanders the world, we'll lose all contact. If we part now, the worst is that we may never see each other again in this lifetime.
Not yet. Anyway, I'll just wander around aimlessly for now and see where I end up.
Sister Xiang, have you decided where you want to go?
Is that so... then I'll have to set off again.
Before long, this place was no longer the Tang Clan.
Are you here to persuade me to leave?

She's just like her father, both of them fond of speaking in such a way. How come I've cultivated a set of martial arts skills, just having a reputation, yet my speech remains so common and vulgar? Is this perhaps a talent for becoming a great hero?
Stinky Younger Brother, why are you ruining the atmosphere! It's rare to have such a Jianghu vibe.
Hey, stop‑don't make it sound like I'm going to duel you.
You came after all
I'm here
You're here
Your cry echoed through the valley, lingering for a long time before finally fading. But there was only silence‑no one replied; perhaps the person from those years was already gone.
If you're going to be disappointed in me, there's nothing I can do. I'm only a mortal and have no supernatural powers ‑ I really did my best...

If you want to be disappointed in me, there's nothing I can do. I'm just an ordinary mortal with no supernatural powers; otherwise I'd have sent a bolt of lightning to force the authorities to replace that official.
I, your junior, followed your instructions and have already repaid the Tang Clan. From now on I owe them nothing, and I don't owe you either!
I, your junior Zhao Huo, have already given my all and stood by you to the end; it's just that Heaven did not grant our wishes.
Masked senior who dwells in seclusion in the mountains!

I used to always hide here and train alone. I didn't want them to see me practicing martial arts from another sect ‑ I was afraid of being mocked, and I wanted my fellow Brothers to see me in a new light. I know every blade of grass and every tree here better than anyone.
...Having paid my respects to Senior Brother, I should be going now.
Come here. Let your master hold an umbrella for you‑after the rain the sky will clear.

I only look down on those cold‑blooded people who can grin and joke while bidding farewell to their hometown and parting from their family. Feelings of tender admiration are natural to everyone; there is no need to feel ashamed of them.
I'm not afraid of you scolding me; I'm only afraid of you looking down on me.
When you do something wrong, I, as your teacher, naturally won't go easy on you. But being attached to one's family‑what sort of wrongdoing is that?
You're not going to scold me?
If you want to cry, then cry ‑ what's the point of hiding it? Do you think I, as your teacher, am so insensitive to people's feelings that I could still scold you?
No, not at all
What, are you crying?
Master
Disciple...
Those good times, in the blink of an eye, have already drifted so far away...
Life is like a journey against the current; I am but a traveler. It's time to go, it's time to go.
Pleasant dreams seldom linger; I alone hesitate
...Not much longer now before I have to say goodbye to Tang Jia Dayuan. I can no longer clearly remember what my childhood home looked like; I only remember the outer fort and the main courtyard.

I don't know whether the Little Junior Sister is comfortable in her married life, whether she's had enough to eat or is staying warm. In any case, it's better that someone's protecting her than having her wander around with the rest of us ‑ a pack of forlorn dogs.
...When I went to the female disciple's room, it wasn't proper or aboveboard ‑ I went because the master's wife had asked me to.
I'll take care of you~
I only have two hands and two legs; if there's too much, I really can't carry it.
See you in a little while, Brother. Your beloved Sister is going back to pack her things ‑ and of course you'll be the one to carry them for me.
Hehe, my good days have arrived ‑ I'll give you a hug as a reward.
I'll do my best‑at least I won't spank you.

Let me state this again, solemnly: I'm hard to take care of. The things my Brother spoiled me with‑you'll have to keep all of them if you take over. I want to eat well and dress well; when I travel there must be a sedan chair and a carriage. If there's neither, you'll have to carry me on your back.
I can't get it, okay?
Instead, you latched onto me. Want to run? Not a chance.

Brother, the Tang Clan has been disbanded. From now on, Shang'er will be left with you and my brother. I don't want to keep burdening my brother's life ‑ knowing they're all right is enough; I don't need to be with them all the time.
All right. After we come down the mountain, let's set off to look for him.
Brother, I want to go find my brother. Can you take me?
Admittedly, that's true
No ‑ I've got you eating out of my hand. You pity me deep in your heart and can't help yourself.
Why are you even asking? Are you even the slightest bit worried?
Brother, the Tang Clan has been disbanded. From now on you should take care of me. You wouldn't bully me, would you...?
What have I done to offend this aunt?
That's too much!
All right, pour out what's inside and pickle yourself in it.
I've seen it
Ah‑yes. Do me a favor: move a little farther away and stay over there. Do you see that crock by the kitchen door?
No
I wanted to ask if there's anything I can help you with?
If you even think about making a move on someone else, I won't go easy on you.
No, not at all~
Brother, why are you staring at the female disciple's room? That's a very improper look.
Okay
Then we'll see each other later
Okay
Be careful with the little beads she left you‑keep them safe and don't lose them.
Jewelry box
Come on, take it, take it‑there, that's right.
... I don't want it.
Moling, this is for you ‑ it's a jewel I've treasured. I'm not lending it to you; I'm giving it to you, okay? Only you can have it ‑ after all, we're good friends.
Only the painting Yunshang left me: pretty marbles... beads... beads...
Hmm, I don't have anything to collect
Little Junior Sister, have you packed up all your things?
Hmm, I'll find you
Is that so? You're really impressive; I have nowhere to hide.
Although I'm flattered and taken aback, in broad daylight it's not good for us to be so affectionate. Third Senior Brother would probably swing his weapon and hit my face.
Good heavens...
To blind you
May I ask, Female Hero, what are you doing?
Like this?
Really? Senior Brother, could you stand a little lower?
Really? I can always vaguely sense you arriving too. We must have a telepathic connection.
...No, it's nothing, just a feeling.

Don't tell us he's not so bad ‑ that's just you seeing him through lover's eyes; you don't mind. Just because you like him doesn't mean we're okay with it. Show us some respect, will you? Either poke out his eyes, or press your body against his to block his sight ‑ don't let him stand out there staring like a fool.
But Senior Brother‑he...
I know he meant no harm; he came for you. But the way his eyes darted around so furtively made everyone terribly uneasy ‑ you could even call it chilling.
Little Junior Sister, could you rein in your Senior Brother Zhao?
That's because...
It's not that I didn't‑I wanted to see you, but I didn't say anything. How did you know I was here?
Um, no
Senior Brother, are you looking for me?

So if I run into thoughtless people of the Wulin on the road and accidentally damage property, that shouldn't count as an offense against heavenly virtue. It's different from killing, so I shouldn't have to pay with my life.
Who said they were foolish and incompetent? Wasn't that move pretty ruthless?
The Wulin Alliance wasn't even an enemy of the Tang Clan; it was merely a large weapon, and the one wielding the sword was the ruling court.
People are the same: if they haven't grown a brain, they're little different from objects‑just pushed along by the winds and currents of the Jianghu.

Over the generations, the Tang Clan's artisans have created countless items. Some benefited their homeland, while others brought disaster to the world, and for that they have often been criticized. But how can objects themselves be labeled righteous or evil? Good people use them for good; villains use them for evil.
The Tang Clan's short swords and Hidden Weapons‑whether iron or wooden‑are all forged here.
You're very sad, aren't you? I'm sorry‑I can't help you in the slightest; I'm a useless woman. If you're hurt, then cry; at least I can stay with you.
Ah...
Good, good

You're really leaving home, so it's understandable ‑ it's okay to cry. If you're sad, just let yourself cry; I'll stay with you. Once you've finished crying, you can be strong again in front of others.
...What does it matter?
Oh‑men may have tears, but they don't let them fall easily; you mustn't be crying and sobbing like that.
I'm glad it's nothing... I was afraid you'd be hurt and upset.
Hm? What's wrong with me?
I did hear about it... are you okay?
Didn't you hear? We're all retiring from the Jianghu‑what are you still fighting for?
What are you doing? Strike while the iron's hot‑I'm halfway through hammering it.
Xiao Zhu, Xiao Zhu, don't knock yet

Yes ‑ we even used to bet on when they'd be driven off in a rage. A month, two months, a year, two years ‑ in the end it just dragged on until today. If Third Senior Brother doesn't put out the lights, I'm afraid they'd still be too reluctant to leave.
...He really saw it through to the end, didn't he.
You go ahead and chat; I'll wander around on my own.
Yeah...
No matter what, as long as we're alive, there's always a chance we'll meet again. Even if we don't get around much, it's nice to write a letter during the holidays.
You're right ‑ I hadn't thought this through before; I still need to consult with my wife.

Who told you, with nothing better to do, to go and snatch someone else's faction leader's throne? Now it's a hot potato you can't get rid of. If you keep being so irresponsible, you'll find out how serious it is when you're wanted by the authorities.
I've retired into seclusion, and the Kongtong Sect still doesn't know how to explain it. Sigh.
Please, we entrust everything to you. Even if the Tang Clan disbands, we want the Little Junior Sister to be well‑she is the Tang Clan's last true heir.
Do you even need to tell me that? I'll protect her for the rest of her life.
What are you muttering over there? I heard you!
For the Little Junior Sister's future, shouldn't we take him out now? Kill this guy, then persuade the Little Junior Sister to find someone reliable.
I will do bad things in the future. I guarantee I'll dispose of the bodies and leave no trace‑without the slightest slip‑up! I won't implicate Little Junior Sister.
Don't worry, don't worry‑how could that be?
Senior Martial Brother, although I don't know what vicious tricks you've used, since you brought Little Junior Sister along you must not drag her into any wrongdoing.
She has stabbed a needle into my heart; I'm afraid it will never heal in my lifetime. I'm destined to endure torment, bleeding drop by drop until I die.
Senior Brother... haven't you come to terms with it yet?
Don't worry, I trust her
That's not right ‑ wherever I go, I'm not confident!
That makes sense. So I won't go to Jiangnan‑where would be safe for me? ... Tufan? Menggu?
Whoever dares lay a finger on my girl, I'll turn Jiangnan's misty rains red.

Putting aside any questions about her character, Sister Ye Xiao, judged by looks alone, is a peerless beauty of the age. In a few years she'll likely become even more beautiful. Jiangnan is full of charming, talented scholars‑aren't you afraid you won't be able to restrain yourself around her?
They want to go east to Jiangnan to take a look; Yunshang longs for the water towns there.
You even forgot you still have a female master to serve‑she harms others and is both jealous and hateful. Why won't Xiahou, the female hero, come and enslave me?
It doesn't necessarily have to be Snow Mountain ‑ what matters is that it's a place where my master can be comfortable.
Being self‑sufficient is fine, but why insist on going to such a bitter, freezing place like the snowy mountains?
Maybe move to the snowy mountains and live as a reclusive hunter. Harbor no great ambitions and be self‑sufficient.
That's out of the question! Don't try to intimidate me!
Are you talking about Lady Shangguan? Senior Brother, you're dreaming. If I were her, the moment I found out you were this useless, I'd abandon you and remarry someone else.
Perhaps I'll try going into business; later in life I'll still have to rely on my wife.
Detestable!
Then you should hide in the back kitchen‑don't show your face, or the customers will lose their appetite.
Maybe they'll open a restaurant and cook
That's great ‑ you seem like you were born to be in this line of work.
Maybe they'd be a carpenter, a blacksmith, or an artisan.
I haven't decided yet
Senior Brother, how about you?

Hey, who hasn't gone through a bit of youthful rebellion? I didn't want to live a mediocre life ‑ I heard Mister Shu's Jianghu Tales would get your blood boiling, so I joined the Tang Clan. But look at me now; I've ended up like this, I'm a bit older, and I figure it's better to go home and settle down.
So it turns out you still have a family business to inherit‑why did you even bother coming to apprentice?
Me too. My family runs a Dyeing Workshop over in Zizhou; business is doing quite well, and Father and Mother are both hoping I'll inherit it.
I left the Tang Clan; maybe I won't be part of the Jianghu anymore. I'm planning to go back to my hometown in Juzhou to see what my relatives are up to, then slowly figure out how to make a living.
What does everyone plan to do? Join another sect or gang?

Third Senior Brother has always been unswervingly loyal to the sect; making this decision was something they had no choice about. No one is obliged to die for anyone else. We were brought together by fate, and now it's time for everyone to go their separate ways.
Hits the nail on the head
That's true... for example, you.
If they don't disband, there will always be someone who won't give up.
Brother... we've all heard that the Brother Sect Leader really intends to dissolve the Tang Clan?
Fine ‑ it's not like we're no longer Brothers; that doesn't mean we can't still meet up and eat together.
After lights‑out, once we descend the mountain, let's go together and have a good meal.
Really? That's great!
If you can wait, I'll cook a simple dish right away‑though I can't promise it'll be very tasty.
Oh... all right, I'll just have to put up with it for now.
I just came in to take a look and reminisce; I wasn't preparing any food.
Junior Brother, I'm so glad you're here. Do you have anything to eat?

Thanks to my Brothers constantly coming up with new ways to make life difficult for me, I'm not short on dishes I can cook. If I stay out of the Jianghu and just be a cook running a restaurant to make a living, that doesn't seem so bad.
Practice makes perfect; before long I'll be able to cook a few signature dishes.
Even if it doesn't taste good, at least it didn't poison anyone.
No one taught me specifically; I just copied what others did ‑ after all, clumsy hands would get beaten. Before I knew it, the old hands were gone, and it was my turn to take charge of the cooking.
...At the busiest times, the kitchen was like a battlefield every day. When things got overwhelming, I would be called in and ordered around by the senior brothers and sisters.
Good heavens!
What do you think? I, Mei, would love to bite a chunk out of you.
Wait ‑ you must be joking, right? You wouldn't actually want to eat that, would you?
Haha
Wahaha~ I, Mei, have my eye on your heart‑I want to dig it out and eat it.
I have no power or influence, no money or standing ‑ I really don't know what you see in me.
I was thinking, why don't I learn face‑changing from you? Even if it can't give you a whole new face, at least tidy you up a bit so you won't look so repulsive. Never mind ‑ this will do.

Ah‑don't be like that‑Xiao Mei was only joking with you‑so petty. I won't say anything, I won't take revenge. As for whether you become the sect leader, it doesn't matter. Marry a chicken, follow the chicken; marry a dog, follow the dog‑anyway, good sir, please don't drive me away.
I've retired from Jianghu, and naturally I won't show my face in Kongtong. If you think I'm ugly, why don't you‑

Mei is narrow‑minded; when someone bullies them, they have to get revenge. Besides, you're already really ugly, and you keep wearing that sour‑puss face all day ‑ it just makes people angry to look at.
No. Even if we manage it, it won't change anything ‑ it would only put both our lives at risk.
You're still talking about this, huh?
If you really can't let it go ‑ so upset you can't even eat or drink ‑ how about after we come down the mountain we disguise ourselves and go assassinate the Wulin Alliance leader or Lord Shangguan?

Bai Mei also hated those groups in the Wulin who constantly spouted about righteousness and morality. Jinxiang Palace followed the Human Path‑so what of it? Those people were afraid to die yet still wanted to be seen as heroes, striking first and crying out for battle. They relentlessly pressed their demands without any mercy. Such character is no more noble than that of the Supreme Bliss Sect.
But that won't work
I hate them‑how I wish I could kill every one of those bastards and fight to the very end, only then would my courage not be wasted.
...of course, they were full of complaints and had to vent.
A'Huo, do you hate me?
That's fine

We're not in any hurry to leave. Even condemned prisoners get a last meal. These rations would just go to waste if left alone, so we might as well cook it all up and let everyone eat their fill before we set off.
Xiaomei, we're about to go down the mountain‑why don't you go pack?
...How did it come to this?

However, the Sect Leader, keen‑eyed and discerning, uncovered the true culprit and beat the First Senior Brother nearly to death. That year, the relationship between Second Senior Brother and the First Senior Brother wasn't yet so bad, so Second Senior Brother pleaded on the First Senior Brother's behalf.

These are the scribbles First Senior Brother made in the book when they were little; they stuffed it back on the shelf, eagerly hoping someone would find it. The meanest part is they even signed it Tang Zheng, trying to pin the blame on Second Senior Brother.
This place is always a mess. I've resolved several times to tidy up, but whenever the weather's nice I open the windows to air the books, and it all gets messy again.
So you were planning to beat me up a lot?!
In your dreams! If I beat you one less time a day, that would already make up for it! Get lost!
How can I make it up to you? Can I live off you?
Zhao Huo... I'm partly responsible for the regrets you carry. From now on I'll slowly make it up to you; I only hope you can let go.
No matter how you look at it, the regret won't go away.
No, leave such trivial matters to me. You're about to leave home ‑ go see the world; don't leave any regrets.
Is there anything I can help you with?
I'm very gratified that you understand my intentions.
If Miss Ying hadn't stepped forward, Lu Weng might not have been willing to be so generous. It's entirely thanks to Miss Ying that everyone's travel expenses have been taken care of.
Besides, everyone has already received their money and gone, so there's no harm in us making a little profit.
I've already said I don't blame you
We'll come back to redeem it when we have the money. I have not the slightest intention of selling it for a pittance or taking the opportunity to profit‑please don't misunderstand.

...I know that the scriptures and paintings in the Lecture Hall are precious treasures of the Tang Clan. I've discussed this with my elder brother, and we decided that since we can't take the bound books, we'll ask Master Lu to pawn them for cash. We'll then distribute the proceeds among the Tang Clan's senior brothers, junior brothers, sisters, and fellow practitioners as travel expenses.
I'm not blaming you
Whew... you scared me. That's why I hit you ‑ serves you right.
That's too much!

Why would I be afraid of ghosts? I've never done anything to have a guilty conscience, so I'm not scared of ghosts knocking at midnight. Even if there really were ghosts, I'd punch them until their souls scattered. But the problem is you are solid and corporeal‑you're a monster!
I did ‑ I said just one word and got cut off. It's broad daylight; you're not going to run into ghosts, so why be so panicked?
You're gonna die! When did you start standing behind me?! Can't you say anything?! You damn mute!
Cluck! Wah!
Why are you laughing all sneaky and mysterious... Oh well ‑ it's not like they're on their guard against me. Even if people are wary of me, it's my own fault. Sigh.
Let's go, let's go
Then we'll get to work
You hear the person you love praising you behind your back; you feel both flattered and a little embarrassed.

It's hard to say. Brother Zhao‑put nicely, he's the most loyal person in the world; put less nicely, he's stubborn as can be. No matter how earnestly I tried to persuade him, he clung on and refused to leave, which shows how hard‑headed he is. Once he decides a place is home, he won't go to even the best places, and people are likewise irreplaceable.

It's hard to say. Brother Zhao may be lacking in decency, but when it comes to loyalty there's nothing to fault. No matter how earnestly I pleaded with him, he just stubbornly clung on and refused to leave, which shows how hard‑headed he is. Once someone decides a place is home, they won't go elsewhere even if it's better; the same goes for people ‑ they're irreplaceable.
He has a beloved wife and is so content he no longer thinks of home‑how would he think of us?

On that day, you inherited the ancestral precepts and resolved to fight to the end. The Tang family's path was destined to be proud and untamed.
Fight their mother!
Fight their mother!
Fight their mother!
Exactly, let us uphold the Tang Clan's valor and fight their mother!
What choice is there? Here lies the meaning of our roaming the Jianghu, the integrity by which we stand. If we run, even if we live, it would be no different from being dead.

The Tang Clan's seniors walk the Jianghu on sheer spirit, staying true to their original purpose and caring little for praise or blame. I, Tang Sheng, though only a bookish scholar temporarily in charge of the clan, would not dare to bring too much shame on our ancestors.
Deal!
I want to get myself back on my feet. If I still have the strength, I'll help arrange placements for our fellow disciples ‑ would that be all right?
...Sigh

Don't blame yourself ‑ on the contrary, it makes it easier for us to leave. You'll be the one left to clean up the mess afterward. Your connections are broader than mine; across the whole sect, only you could pull it off.

But I'm serious‑Third Senior Brother, it was only because you insisted that I reluctantly gave my opinion. If things really turn disastrously, I won't throw my life away for nothing. I'm not joking at all, so don't blame me for being heartless then.
The majority rules; I don't have anything more to say.
Don't even think about it
I thought my single vote wouldn't make a difference, so I voted casually. This is bad... Is it still possible to take it back now?
Since we've lost, we'll accept defeat. Besides, this was always a matter for the sect leader to decide.
There was nothing I could do; might makes right, so I had to accept defeat.
Don't say it like you weren't involved
I've long suspected you weren't quite right; seeing you today, you really do live up to your reputation.

So the final conclusion is to resist to the end‑no further objections?
Alright, then the junior brother's opinion will count as two votes.

I guess this counts as... an abstention.
Junior Brother, don't praise her so recklessly‑you're spoiling her too much!

Little Junior Sister, how about you?

Fight their mother

Has everyone made up their minds? Let's get some paper and pens, write down our answers individually, and then reveal them together.
Burdened with worries, you tossed and turned until dawn, still deeply anxious.
No need to repay, the Abbot said. Helping the Tang Clan is repaying you on behalf of the people.
Abbot, your noble generosity‑this kindness, I truly don't know how to repay.
I hereby send this humble monk, accompanied by a few fellow Brothers, to help defend. If the Wulin Alliance intends to act against the Tang Clan, I can also say a few fair words to reason with them.

Abbot Master Fangzhu greatly esteemed Old Palm Leader Tang and our former alliance with Songshan in expelling evil. Knowing the Tang Clan's proud spirit, he doubts they would submit to the Wulin Alliance. Fearing potential strife between us, he worries about impending calamity.
Exactly ‑ they insisted on helping
Are you insisting on helping?
Even if Sect Leader Tang refuses to accept it, we will still register to stay at the town temple.
That's thoughtful of you

I, this monk, later explained everything to that elderly person in detail; they too regretted their earlier actions and repeatedly apologized. They therefore specially sent me to offer an apology and brought several Brothers to help guard the Tang Clan. If the Wulin Alliance intends to act against the Tang Clan, they can also speak a few fair words to dissuade them.

The Abbot has been cultivating Buddhist teachings in seclusion; his mind is entirely clear, and he is not versed in worldly scheming. When he, the elderly person, asked you to stay, he hadn't thought about the consequences at all. He simply believed that if everyone sat down, had a cup of tea and spoke openly, there would be no problem‑he had no malice whatsoever.
But your Songshan Sect wasn't on our side either back then.
Amituofo. Elder Benefactor Tang, long time no see; I only ran into Benefactor Zhao a short while ago.

Before any pleasantries, this humble monk must say solemnly: Dharma Master Shi Ming's words and actions have nothing to do with Songshan. I ask everyone to look into this carefully and not to blame a good person.
Good Fortune──
Please, all venerable monks of Songshan, ascend the mountain.
Hurry‑bring them up the mountain!
If I don't shout a few words first, I can't attract everyone's Attention. I want everyone to direct their Attention to me.
They're being so polite ‑ what are you still making a fuss about?
No, not at all ‑ they were very polite; after I left, they just sat in the teahouse drinking tea.
Are they intending to force their way in?
It's Monk Fu Yun, accompanied by a group of brawny monks from the Songshan sect!
I just took off my shoes and socks. Who's come‑why so nervous?
No, this is bad! Someone's here! Where's Brother Zhao? Wake up, don't sleep!

I'll be your hostage ‑ to hold the Beggar... the Beggar Sect in check. Once I disappear, the Beggar Sect's new and old factions will start fighting, and the alliance leader will have to take responsibility to mediate. That way, we can‑can buy time to recruit troops!

That's right ‑ they stood toe‑to‑toe with the Wulin Alliance acting under orders from the Imperial Court; the two alliances were locked in a standoff. As long as the deadlock held, the Imperial Court couldn't play one off the other and then discard them.
West‑West Wulin Alliance...! Just like before, under Lord Yue's banner there was a Civil Alliance Leader for the Western Thirteen Provinces and a Martial Hegemon for the Eastern Thirteen Provinces?
Xiao Ju's best course of action... Leader Wang and Lady Wen had already thought of it long ago!
I have come here to reveal the strategy planned by Gang Master Wang and Lady Wen‑to establish a Western Wulin Alliance centered around the Tang Clan!
...When Alliance Leader Nangong perished, I thought the path to peace had ended ‑ but it hadn't. The mutual trust between Alliance Leader Rui and Young Hero Zhao Zhao Zhao is the new bridge.

Idiot ‑ do you think I have the time to play tricks with you? People have basic needs; officials and beggars alike have to poop. Anyone who can't poop is the real freak! I tell you something and you just keep asking and asking ‑ are you ever going to stop?
Huh‑?! Weren't you in the middle of a poop‑escape?
Oh, fuck ‑ I'll come back and tell you the details after I'm done.
Huh?
Then you'll have to endure hardship ‑ go to the Tang Clan as a hostage.
Heh, you finally asked a good question
...What if everything that was just said happens, but I insist on fighting shoulder to shoulder with my friends from the Tang Clan?
Wait‑I'll ask one more thing, just one
Alright. Ask me one more question and I'll‑I've been a hero my whole life‑I'll end up shitting my pants!

Before becoming a great hero, you are first and foremost a person‑nothing to be ashamed of. Your body and hair are given by your parents; someone who doesn't cherish themselves isn't worthy of being a hero at all.
So... like that, can one still be called a xia?

Get as far away as you can. Take the Beggar Sect members and leave the Central Plains. Don't concern yourself with the Tang Clan or any lofty Datong ideals. Make sure the Beggar Sect members have food and shelter; if you can't even look after the people around you, then just look after yourself.
Flee

But, Foster Father, what if you're wrong? What if I do everything I can and still can't protect the Nangong family head? What if the Nangong family head becomes the alliance leader but refuses to offend the Imperial Court for the sake of the Tang Clan?
If you've pretty much asked enough, go back to your nest and sleep‑don't bother people while they're pooping.

...How can one have it both ways? Either choice is difficult; whether I stay or go, there will be regrets. I'm already the head of the Beggars; living like a beast, it can't get any worse ‑ so I might as well shoulder the dung and take it with me.
Adoptive Father, don't you feel any regret?
I will. This is something we agreed on together, and each of us will bear our own consequences. My relationship with her is a matter for our generation; you don't need to worry about it.
But will Lady Wen agree to Great Hero Nangong becoming the alliance leader?
So you must do as I say
That won't do!

No one dares to defy the Imperial Court to uphold justice. Scholars will increase, while chivalrous warriors who wish to learn martial arts will dwindle, eventually leading to the loss of martial arts. From then on, aristocrats will act without restraint, the poor will become poorer, and the rich will grow richer. If they can't support beggars, they will kill all beggars.
After the collapse...?

During the Imperial Court's conciliatory period they wouldn't move against the Tang Clan, but once that period ended they'd most likely burn the bridge and settle old scores. Having that prior lesson as a warning, no one in the Wulin dared to resist the Imperial Court anymore. Once the balance was broken, the situation would collapse.
...because, apart from the Nangong family head, no one in the world could protect the Tang Clan.
Yes... this child understands.
You must put the bigger picture first; you must never say that kind of defeatist talk again.
How I wish I could take back the words I said back then...
...I'm the one who killed your father, remember? You loudly declared you'd kill me sooner or later to avenge him. Now that I'm giving you the chance, why do you look so reluctant to strike?
Anyway, before long my adoptive father will abandon me. I'll be an orphan again; if I don't ask him now, there won't be another chance.
You'll have to figure it out for yourself sooner or later. How old are you, still acting spoiled?
I'm dull‑witted; I just can't make sense of it. I'm simply afraid that if I can't think it through thoroughly and can't be flexible, it'll only make things worse.
You sure have a lot of questions
Why must it be the head of the Nangong family?

If I'm not mistaken, the Nangong family head‑the people's choice‑will surely become the alliance leader. If I am mistaken, you must still find a way to bring it about. Therefore you must be patient and only speak up at the crucial moment.

Chances are they'll call another Wulin Grand Assembly then ‑ people of the Jianghu love a spectacle, and this plays to that. Electing a single alliance leader to keep the Wulin in check is easier than coaxing each sect into submission.
You've unified the Beggar Sect‑what now?

You will take on the role of the Beggar Sect's Sect Master. Calm the old generation and keep them within the sect, preventing them from acting recklessly outside its bounds. You must be submissive and mediate between the new and old factions to ease their conflicts. Drag this situation out until all the elders have passed away, then take over the power of the old faction and unify the Beggar Sect.
So... so... so... what should I do?

No. This is the necessary path to Great Harmony; members of the Wulin can also put their skills to use in serving the state. Conversely, if relations between the Imperial Court and the people are not reconciled now, once the external threat is removed the Wulin will inevitably face a purge by the Imperial Court.
Is this a bad thing?
After the Jiangling Action, the Imperial Court, having perceived a chance to coexist with Jianghu forces, will certainly take conciliatory measures and actively court figures within the Wulin.

So our surrounding of Jiangling was not aimed at victory, but at stirring up the Jianghu, breaking the established order, and forcing those sunk in indulgence and clinging to old rules to grow tense and set their minds to work‑

The Great Song's resistance to the Jin has already been stretched beyond its limits; its main forces are deployed on the frontier, leaving no strength to pacify the interior. If another rebellion breaks out, the Great Song's fate will be sealed.
Child, keep firmly in mind what your sworn father said today.
Brother, my visit is precisely about this matter.

Master Shi Ming stepping forward to accuse you plays exactly into the Imperial Court's hands. They didn't move against you at the Wulin conference; later they certainly won't let you off. Our humble sect's former leader, Wang, predicted all this long ago.

There is no need to align with you; it is already sufficient to sigh. I have heard that the Wulin Alliance intends to cause you trouble, and he is very unwilling about it. But you know well that the court originally wanted to target you as well, just lacking a pretext, fearing that provoking an incident might spark common outrage.
Sigh, every family has its own troubles
Ah... come to think of it, so that's how it was. I thought they had left already ‑ it turns out they were absent because of this? That's a bit too...

At Jinxiang Palace, when the Tang Clan was being accused, the alliance leader was driven off by his own wife and took refuge outside. Several of his wives were squabbling, vying for his favor, and it even turned physical. He spent a long time calming them down before he returned.
At Alliance Leader Rui's inauguration banquet, upon hearing that the Tang Clan had‑had‑been accused by Master Shi Ming, they crushed their wine cups and urgently tried to persuade everyone.

Not siding with you, and standing on your opposite side, is already sufficient to lament. I have also heard that the Wulin Alliance intends to cause you trouble, and he is very unwilling about it. But you know well enough that the court originally wanted to target you as well, only worrying about lacking a valid pretext; they feared that rashly provoking you might stir up common resentment.
Every family has its own problems
Ah... come to think of it, so that's how it was. I even thought he had left earlier‑so he was absent because of this?
When the incident at Jinxiang Palace occurred, Alliance Leader Rui was in the midst of a family dispute. Their worries arose from love ‑ after all, even heroes struggle with matters of the heart.
He said he and Brother Zhao are friends who would give their lives for each other. He can stake his reputation on the fact that you are absolutely not a member of the Mud Cult.

At Alliance Leader Rui's inauguration banquet, they heard that the Tang Clan had been accused. Deeply shocked, they did their utmost to persuade the two Lords and the sect leaders to urge the Gang Leader to think twice and stay calm.
Although it ended up like this, I intended to support the Tang Clan. This may sound like an evasive excuse, but please hear me out.
The Beggar Sect has always supported the Tang Clan.
At the time of the Wulin gathering, for various reasons it simply wasn't the right time. Now the time is ripe.
They came to help
That's right. My adoptive father, unlucky in love in his youth, ran ‑ ran off to Songshan intending to be ordained as a monk. In the end he never got his head shaved; instead, he ended up like this.
King Hongpeng ‑ the martial overlord of the Eastern Thirteen Prefectures who follows Lord Yue!
Leader Wang is a secular disciple of Songshan and the inheritor of Spring Sleep Master. Spring Sleep Master is none other than ──
All right, that's enough. I came on this trip precisely to say that.
...Now that it's come to this, you can say it, right?
Then why did you come together with Leader Li?
No need to repay, the Abbot said. Helping the Tang Clan is repaying you on behalf of the people.
Abbot, your noble generosity‑this kindness, I truly don't know how to repay.
I hereby send this humble monk, accompanied by a few fellow Brothers, to help defend. If the Wulin Alliance intends to act against the Tang Clan, I can also say a few fair words to reason with them.

Exactly ‑ they insisted on helping
