The place he is going to is even farther than the Xiangyang battlefield, located in Bianjing. To address the root of the problem, we must remove the heads of the Jin Emperor Wanyan Xun and the Jin Commander Shuhu Gaoqi from their necks. This means removing the heads of the Golden Country's Emperor Wanyan Xun and General Su Hu Gaoqi.
To put it simply, the warriors and officials of Song Kingdom are stretched thin‑able to feel the urgency but lacking in resources to act. Only those who wander freely can undertake such a task. When it comes to the wandering hero, there is none more suitable for an assassination than Flying Hero Tang Buyi. To cut off the root of the war, who else but him?

Master Nangong of the Nangong family has thanked your senior brother and yourself for saving his son. He inquired about the whereabouts of your eldest senior brother. To avoid arousing suspicion, you lied and said that he had gone to the pleasure house to enjoy himself.\nNangong Yuan was taken aback for a moment, then burst into laughter. In his younger days, he too had been a charming and dashing young lord, even if he considered his reputation and kept himself pure, he still needed to hear the music and touch the delicate hands of the little miss before he would be satisfied.\nOriginally, I was a bit concerned about your senior brother being too self‑centered and not even bothering with a few polite words. But upon hearing that he went to the pleasure house, I immediately felt relieved. With a satisfied expression of someone who has been through it all, I smiled and walked away.
The family head frowned upon hearing this, though he did not scold, he was displeased with your master brother's independent nature, not even offering a few polite words, which was quite impolite.
Nangong Family Head thanked you and your master's brothers for saving his son, and inquired about the whereabouts of your master's elder brother. To avoid suspicion, you pretended not to know.

Wang Erzhuang then proceeded to recount his efforts in detail.
What he plans in his heart far exceeds what you could imagine.
Originally, Gang Leader Wang was deeply concerned about his country and home. He also had a profound understanding of the Jianghu. The grudges between the court and the past were like ice three feet deep, not thawed in just one day. Calculating it all, it turns out that it's been several generations of officials who owe the people of the Jianghu more than they realize.
Unless all those who know the old tales of the Jianghu perish, or there is a change of dynasty with the country replaced by new rulers, the court and the Jianghu will forever be like oil and water, irreconcilable.  Translation: Unless all those who know the old tales in the Jianghu perish, or there is a change of dynasty with the country replaced by new rulers, the court and the Jianghu will forever be like oil and water, irreconcilable. One cannot expect the Jianghu to produce another Great Hero Nangong Zhi to sacrifice himself for his country and people, nor can one hope for an Alliance Leader in civil affairs to assist Marshal Yue as there was in the past.
The Nangong family maintains good relations with the officialdom above while not shunning alliance with the common folk below. Given time, Old Master Nangong Heng's idea of a great unification could potentially reverse this situation. However, since everything cannot be perfect immediately, it is best to deliberate carefully and never rush into anything hasty.
But with the nation in peril, the Jin people will not wait for you to unite before launching another invasion. Meanwhile, soldiers are sacrificing their lives on the frontier every day.
For now, the only course of action is to deliver a rude awakening, sound the alarm, and attack the Jiangling garrison. By invoking the face of the Nangong family, we can draw in support from major sects within the Wulin. Using this as a fait accompli, we compel the court to rely on the forces of the Jianghu; otherwise, with the fall of Jiangling, Xiangyang will lose its reliance, and the nation's stability will be at risk.
After speaking, you and the Senior Brother both solemnly showed mutual respect, taking out cups and drinks to silently toast. After finishing the drink, you gave each other a respectful bow as Wang Erzhuang stepped away. Tonight's farewell; next time we meet, we will be foes again.
The more admiring you are of him, the more you should oppose him to rally the people's hearts. Because the real enemy is still watching from outside Xiangyang with bated breath.
The Gang Master's grand scheme involves enemies, not friends.
He has already decided his own path and allows no one to walk it with him.
There's no way to think of it, so Wang Erzhuang can only roll up his sleeves and personally step in to beat you.

You have practiced your martial arts diligently and are not entirely helpless. Seeing Wang Erzhuang's gaze directed at you, you moved instinctively to avoid the flying hook. However, Nangong Qian lacks your skill; he was drawn close by Wang Erzhuang, who then knocked him out with a single palm strike.\nDon't look at you as just an ordinary person and treat you with indifference; Wang Erzhuang and Senior Brother have already taken a second look at you. You see, Wang Erzhuang's fishing rod may not be very effective for catching fish, but he has never failed when it comes to catching people. Being able to avoid his hook means your skills are truly formidable.

Before that, however, it's necessary to deal with all the irrelevant people. By irrelevant people, I naturally mean you.\nWang Erzhuang said nothing and threw out the fishing rod. You and Nangong Qian were surprised and tried to dodge, but two hooks simultaneously clung to your collars, pulling you forward against your will. A single palm each took care of you cleanly and efficiently.

The two black‑robed figures removed their masks simultaneously, revealing the person opposite to be your senior brother, Tang Buyi. As for the man behind you, it was none other than Dharma King Wang Erzhuang from the Beast Path, who is currently leading thousands of Beggar Sect disciples in a fierce battle with the orthodox Wulin at Jiangling!
Now that he has shown his true form, Wang Erzhuang dismissed the idea of hiding his techniques. He let you go; after all, if he wanted to take your life again, he could simply act on it. Besides, he seems to have some connection with your senior brother.
Once classmates who shared drinks and fostered a generational friendship, they are now enemies.
Senior Master Brother opened the door and immediately asked why he had surrounded the city. Given his abilities, it was inconceivable that he would surround the city for a Jianghu dispute without thought or provoking the court.
Wang Erzhuang saw his senior brother analyze the situation with great insight and was quite relieved. He rejoiced at the prospect of the Jianghu having this new talent. Recalling the old debt he owed for a drink, he decided to openly share his previously undisclosed plans with him.

Hold on to your black‑clothed assassin; just from our brief engagement, I managed to discern their technique. Their words are astonishing, declaring that the person across must be from your Tang Clan. The black‑clothed assassin scoffed in response, refusing to admit it and instead accusing them of being the lightning hero from the Pleasure House.\nThe moment you heard those words, you immediately believed that the person across from you was undoubtedly the Senior Brother. Furthermore, his words were reckless and unfiltered, suggesting that he intentionally wanted to kill you.\nLittle did she know that the black‑clothed man who captured her was greatly shaken by the news and actually revealed his true form voluntarily.

Holding onto the black‑robed figure, he had discerned his opponent's style from just their brief encounter, and spoke with startling audacity. He declared that the man across was surely from your Tang Clan. The black‑robed figure sneered in response, unwilling to admit it, instead accusing the other of being Tang Buyi.\nThis tactic backfires very effectively; the black‑clothed person falls silent right away.\nThe black‑cloaked guest was not really afraid, but was unwilling to suffer this injustice. He thus removed his mask, revealing his true face.

Hold on to your black‑robed figure; just from our brief encounter earlier, I could discern your style. Your words are astonishing, claiming that the person across from you must be from the Tang Clan. He sneered in response, refusing to admit it and instead accusing him of being Nangong Shen.
Nangong Shen is Nangong Qian's older brother, yet they are treated as if they come from different mothers. He has never looked favorably upon his younger brother and rarely gives him a second glance at home. Yet, it seems he would never go so far as to harbor thoughts of killing his brother either.
Upon hearing this, Nangong Qian's heart instantly felt a chill. Not that she didn't believe it, but rather that she was unwilling to accept it.
The person saw his despondent appearance and could only sigh internally before revealing their true form.

You and Nangong Qian immediately employed qinggong to chase them out of the city. Once you reached the outskirts, you saw the two opponents relying on faint starlight to listen for and judge each other's moves, exchanging blows at breakneck speed. In an instant, they had exchanged dozens of martial arts techniques and separated, each taking a corner.   But you and Nangong Qian, having rashly approached without leaving any room for a counterattack, were suddenly caught off guard as both of you were grabbed by the same opponent, held hostage.\nNangong Qian, despite not being favored at home, is still a noble young lord from a prominent family. As for you, even if he squeezes out every last bit of value, it might not amount to the worth of Nangong Qian's single fingernail. The moment that black‑clothed man caught you, he felt he had made a significant loss.

You and Nangong Qian hurriedly woke up the servants, summoned the head of the household, and informed them about the unexpected visitor's nighttime visit to the Nangong residence.
But while the old patriarch offered some comfort, the other Nangong disciples frowned deeply upon hearing this. Not only were they not concerned about the Second Young Lord's safety, but they even blamed you for disturbing their peaceful dreams in the middle of the night.
Essentially, this group of people fundamentally doesn't believe that anyone dares to launch a night raid on the Nangong Family in these parts. If there were such an incident, the night guards would surely be punished. That's why he frantically spread rumors, claiming that it was intentionally false information about the Second Young Lord to draw attention and gain notoriety.
As for the lord of the household, even if he despised this unwanted child, he could not ignore it and sent people immediately to investigate the traces of the two black‑clad men, but unsurprisingly, there was nothing to find.
After this incident, Nangong Qian received even worse treatment from the nobility. No one bothered to interact with him, treating him as if he were invisible.
As a result, even you are considered complicit. The gaze of the aristocrats carries an additional hint of disdain.

A masked figure in black cloaks suddenly appeared on the eastern wall, executing qinggong to leap into the courtyard, locking onto Nangong Qian, ready to strike. Yet before they could act, another masked figure in black cloaks emerged from the western wall, also employing qinggong to enter the courtyard. At first, you assumed the two were allies, but they both hesitated, uncertain, and after a brief standoff, forgot their original intent, clashing with a cacophony of sounds. The fight escalated, pushing them further apart. After you and Nangong Qian escaped unscathed, you remained in a state of bewilderment.

Tonight, you toss and turn in bed not because of any troubling matters, but honestly, since arriving at the Nangong Family Clan, everything is attended to by others. Without having to engage in fights with fellow disciples outside the city, you've been idle and lazy.
With my willpower strengthened and the food so good, it's natural that I'm having trouble sleeping.
Feeling aimless and bored, I decided to take a walk in the cool night air. Arriving at the courtyard, I heard some noise and went closer to investigate‑was it not the Second Young Lord Nangong Qian?

\nYou fell into Di Ao's trap. The rumors of this person holding martial arts competitions to find a wife have spread far and wide, but you had not heard them. You only thought it was just another ordinary competition and easily engaged her in battle, giving her the chance to stick with you. Thankfully, the Sect Leader is sensible and did not promise her to you. Di Ao remains undeterred; he has even become a disciple of the Tang Clan and changed his name to Tang Jiao Jiao. He intends to cultivate feelings for you by getting close, and if that fails, he can always hold another martial arts competition to find a wife. This time, he will use his true skills to defeat you and make you submit.

The Tang Clan is in dire need of revival, and it was precisely the time to recruit new members.\nBut upon further thought, this person is clever and shrewd, with a considerable amount of guile. To keep them in the Tang Clan could potentially lead to nurturing a tiger that brings harm, so I refused.\nTang Shan knelt outside the Tang Clan compound for another night, cultivating hatred from respect. With tears dried, he left the mountain with a resolve: one day, he would make you all regret your decision today.

The Tang Clan is in dire need of revival, and it was precisely the time to recruit new members.\nBut upon reconsideration, this person is clever and shrewd, with a certain depth to their character. Keeping them in the Tang Clan could potentially lead to nurturing a tiger to cause trouble. Therefore, they were refused.\nYou recalled what the Sect Leader had said and spoke up to plead for him, asking to keep him around for observation. You suggested he could do some of the menial tasks you used to handle. As for the other brothers and sisters in cultivation, it was clear they wouldn't treat him kindly. If he couldn't withstand their treatment, he would leave on his own.

Third Senior Brother saw him as a promising individual, his sincere remorse stirred compassion in him. Moreover, the Tang Clan was in dire need of revitalization, precisely the time to recruit talent. Thus, he decided to keep him for observation, assigning him to perform the same menial tasks he used to do. As for the other disciples and siblings, it was clear they would not have a favorable response toward him. If he could not endure, he would leave on his own.

Other accomplices were spared their lives and secretly rejoiced, but only Tang Shan refused to give up, kneeling outside the courtyard gate, claiming he had genuinely reformed and requested to be taken in.

\nAfter the civil war, the Tang Clan in Guangzhou either fled or had their pleas for leniency heard by the Nangong Family, causing the clan to be thrown into turmoil. However, there was no time to deal with these traitors; thus, they could only mete out mild punishment as a warning, ensuring that none of them would dare to set foot in Sichuan again.

Fourth Senior Brother seldom says he is a good person, but he is still rather chivalrous towards his family and friends. Since it's because of your help that I was able to get this money, naturally, I should give you half of it.\nYou couldn't push it away. You mysteriously accepted the money and were afraid he might try to take you out on a high‑interest loan. As a result, you held onto the money without daring to use it yourself, only to eventually believe after some time that you had just overthought it.

Fourth Senior Brother seldom claims to be a good person, but he is still quite chivalrous towards his family and friends. Since it was because of your help that this money came to him, naturally, he should give you half of it.\nYou couldn't refuse it. You oddly accepted the coin and felt their kindness, making your turbid mind somewhat clearer over the consecutive days.

Fourth Senior Brother approached to ask upon seeing the situation. Chao He looked at this man and saw that he was round and chubby with a lovable, simple‑looking face. He figured the man would be easy to deceive and thus already held him in low regard. Fourth Senior Brother then tried his old trick again.  Little did he know that the person in front of him was actually the craftiest member of their sect. The flimsy lies that the man had woven were countered by Fourth Senior Brother, who turned the tables and used them to get what he wanted: Since he has taken on all the tasks from the mountain lately, and Zhao, the junior disciple, is nowhere to be found, then the one who borrowed money from someone yesterday must be Chao He. Isn't that very obvious?\nChao He broke out in a cold sweat and stammered, wanting to argue further. However, Fourth Senior Brother was not like the others who would easily let things slide. There was no way he would give Chao He an opportunity to save face. He exposed all of Chao He's lies and managed to strip him of his money entirely.\nNot enough to cover the debt, those that haven't been settled will continue to accrue interest. As long as Tang Weiyuan is around, Chao He won't be able to have a good life.

You clearly spent a good while getting everything in order before daring to take a breath and do your own thing.\nThat day for some reason, it seemed as though the senior brothers were discussing you and deliberately putting you on the spot.\nYou didn't understand, only feeling a subtle discomfort in your heart.

\nAfter days of hard work, you managed to complete all the major and minor tasks of the household at once, finally finding some respite. After chopping firewood, you were so exhausted that you couldn't even eat a meal and just grabbed a newly steamed bun, planning to nap for a while before waking up to have it.\nYou hadn't been gone for more than a moment when Chao He picked up an axe and pretended to be chopping firewood, even though he had just finished. He acted as if he was utterly exhausted from his exertions. When the fellow brothers and sisters asked him, he boldly claimed that all your hard work over these days fell on his shoulders. The fellow brothers and sisters were taken aback but believed him. They thought it wasn't you who had been working so diligently in and out of the place for several days, but this person, while you were off somewhere enjoying yourself without them knowing where you went.

You couldn't care less about his fruit and that tiny sum of money; you showed no appreciation and turned away.\nHe sees you like this and hates it so much that his teeth itch. With him already inside the room and set to learn the song formulas, given his unparalleled talent, he'll be stepping on your head in no time. By then, you'll be the fake one.

You can't help but envy her. Why didn't your mother ever do something like this for you?\nYou didn't take the money but accepted the honey candies, showing a sign of reconciliation.\nHe didn't appreciate it and sneered coldly, tucking the coin away for himself.

You can see through this person's false sincerity right away; they're certainly not a good person. But you're not an easy target either. He pretends to be generous by offering money, so you should honestly and without hesitation accept it. After all, if you don't take it, he'll definitely accuse you of taking it.

You can't help but envy her. Why didn't your mother do anything like this for you?\nYou accepted the coin and fruit as a sign of reconciliation.\nHe chuckled coldly and gloated with satisfaction. He has regarded you as his top imaginary foe for now. Once he masters the martial arts, you're doomed!

If it were anyone else, such disobedience would have long gotten them expelled from the sect by the Sect Leader.
Unlike the nun, she spent twenty years in the Lecture Hall, working hard and achieving much for the Tang Clan, sacrificing her youth and missing out on her prime. At around forty years old, she finally received a proposal from a widowed man, securing herself a place in life.
The Sect Leader personally promised her one thing: as long as it wasn't something that violated reason or disgraced the family name. The Tang Clan would see to it that she was married off in a grand and honorable manner, accomplishing for her what seemed like an impossible task.
Now that she has returned, she has fulfilled her rare wish for this newly adopted dry son. She is childless, and Chao He calls her Mama, which delights her immensely. All of her love is devoted to him, hoping he will join the Tang Clan and master martial arts, no longer suffering at the hands of others. She commands the disciples of her sect to establish his authority, hiding her savings under sweets and fruits for him to use in winning over his fellow clansmen. Employing both gentle and forceful tactics, she ensures that everyone treats him with renewed respect.

With her command, the disciples lined up in formation and split into two arrays for paired practice, exhausting themselves to the bone.\nThe nun gave the guest a taste of her authority, fully satisfied, and even lazy to point out any more out of idle interest. She took her adopted son to pay respects at the Central Heart Hall to meet the Sect Leader.

She only thought that the person she was selected to appreciate was a master she had trained personally, and would easily be able to discipline you, an outsider disciple who hadn't received true transmission. How could she have expected your unexpected moves? Not only did the senior brother not want to fight in the first place, but even if he really wanted to beat you up, you might not have been his match, resulting in his defeat.\nThe nun was furious but couldn't do anything about it. She thought better of it and decided to go to the Sect Leader and complain about you, accusing you of secretly learning martial arts from other sects. She even suggested that he expel you from the sect.
Using someone else's hands to beat you thoroughly, to vent her anger on her stepson, only then would she feel satisfied, and thus temporarily spare you.

With strong reinforcements and fellow senior brothers being cautious, your side manages to achieve a numerical advantage.
Since Second Senior Brother acted, he wasn't about to let them off so easily. He announced that as of today, they would have to do morning runs around the mountain every day, double their daily assignments, cancel their midday naps, and meditate in the Righteous Heart Hall at night. Monthly exams would now be held every two weeks, and those who failed would have him personally supervise them.
This day probably feels even more torturous than hell, with serving in the military at least offering some hope.
Everyone complained bitterly and the grievances were well‑documented. The Abbess saw that this niece disciple was being extremely ruthless, and feared stirring up public anger. Since her show of authority had already been sufficient, she took her adopted son to pay a visit to the Sect Leader at the Center Mind Hall.

Among the group of disciples, there are a few senior brothers who have been guided by the auntie, and they hold her in particular reverence. Though unwilling to fight you, they were compelled by the auntie's command to spar with you publicly.

She gave the order with the pretense of sparring, intending to summon all the fellow brothers to attack you as a group.\nThe fellow brothers and sisters certainly revered her, but their reverence was greater than their fear. They remembered the hard work she had put in before and thought that occasionally showing off a bit on the mountain and causing some trouble for everyone was acceptable. Now, however, it seemed like an absurd idea to command fellow disciples to attack their own brothers and sisters. Emotionally and logically, it made no sense. Everyone's faces showed anger, and not a single person obeyed her order.\nThe nun had never been publicly contradicted by her fellow sect members. Her face turned a deep red, and she couldn't help feeling anxious. The momentum of her arrogance began to wane, and instead of making a good impression, she might end up messing things up. Thus, she suppressed her anger and took the adopted son to visit the Master of Zhengxin Hall.

The Second Senior Brother has been disturbed for a long time. If the Senior Sister only lightly scolds you a few times, he'd ignore it. But a married Senior Sister ordering disciples to surround and kill fellow disciples is something the sect's rules cannot tolerate. He reluctantly intervenes, also using the opportunity to teach these unreasonable and foolish junior disciples.

Little Junior Sister saw you surrounded from afar and without hesitation joined your side.\nThe Second Senior Brother had been bothered by constant disturbances for a long time, and seeing that the Little Junior Sister stepped forward, he feared she might be harmed due to protecting this worthless fellow. Reluctantly, he intervened to also take the opportunity to discipline these foolish junior brothers who didn't understand proper behavior.

With a single command from her, all the brothers were compelled by her oppressive authority to attack you together, under the guise of sparring, while the Grandmaster seemed intent on taking the opportunity to kill you.

Last time he pulled that off not long ago, but this time Chao He, pretending to be you, climbed the mountain again. This time, he found a powerful patron, and now he walks with such confidence that there's no trace of his previous submissive demeanor from last time.
He sought support from a senior elder who married out of your Tang Clan. Even the Sect Leader addresses her as Senior Sis.
Before Third Senior Brother took over the management of our sect's financial records, this senior nun handled everything. Every time she returned, she would show off her authority and achievements, reprimand junior members, and satisfy her sense of being a senior. This time, however, she went even further, clearly intending to make a strong statement for Dryson by giving him a severe lesson.

You wished he were dead, and you sincerely expressed your desire to kill him.\nThird Senior Brother was shocked and pale, but instead, the Sect Leader actually showed a tone of commendation and encouragement. Although he doesn't approve of you killing him, beating him half to death isn't a big issue.\nEven the headmaster of your sect approves of you beating him. There's no reason for hesitation; grab his collar and take big steps out, toss him outside the courtyard before you start.

You ultimately chose to let it slide, thinking that you are not a person of great renown and that if you had been overly difficult, people might have gossiped about it later. So, you lightly let him go.
Third Senior Brother lightly sent him off down the mountain. Listening to his tearful complaints about his unfortunate fate, Third Senior Brother was moved by compassion and gave him the silver he had saved frugally, hoping he would work hard and not bow to destiny.
Little did he know that the moment he left, Chao He turned around and laughed at him for being easy to deceive, thinking of him as a foolish fool who could be tricked.
Who is this Chao He, then? Just a scumbag, a traitor‑no one tricks wise people, but they specialize in fooling good‑hearted folks like Third Senior Brother.
He didn't care about how his actions would tarnish the last remnants of goodness in the world, making benevolent people less trusting. He just enjoyed himself, had books to read, though he wasn't fond of reading them. And he envied those who did read, wishing that all scholars and wise men would die early and not attain rebirth.

You've been waiting for this sentence. Now, seeing the master himself display a commendatory and encouraging expression, and even the senior disciples of the sect approve of you beating someone, there's no room for hesitation. You grab his collar, take large steps out, throw him outside the courtyard, and then proceed to fight him.
Second Senior Brother then ordered you to go out with him to seek justice for himself.

Upon hearing this, the Second Senior Brother advised the Sect Leader to accept this person as an indoor disciple.
You were shocked and angry. How come, after all your hard work and dedication over the years, you are still an outsider disciple? This person is misusing your reputation to act recklessly. Instead of rebuking him, Second Senior Brother actively recommends that he become a formal disciple?
Gao He has a very thick skin; he immediately wiped away his tears and burst out laughing. Despite receiving such generous treatment, he shows no gratitude and even acts as if he is struggling to do it. This made you so frustrated that you almost pulled out your small sword to fight back right there.
Little did the speaker know that Second Senior Brother had changed the subject and his face was now covered in a frosty demeanor. This was precisely to get this person to submit to the sect. Only then could he deal with him according to sect regulations. At that time, if he didn't torture this hateful person until he suffered greatly, he would take your surname Zhao instead of Tang.
Chao He heard this and immediately became humble again, making various excuses. He also said that his family member had just passed away, making it unsuitable for him to change his sect or surname; he played up his misfortune extensively.
The Second Senior Brother hates to kill you and be done with it, but in comparison, he finds you, this unprecedented and unparalleled self, rather pleasing to the eye.

This person used another's name to commit evil deeds. Although you didn't intend to retaliate harshly, letting him go would still leave you feeling resentful. You also dared not act improperly in front of the sect master, so you consulted Second Senior Brother, the sect's chief executioner.

You couldn't help but resonate with his confession, seeing a reflection of your own humble self in him.
You too have endured similar humiliations, been misunderstood, and deceived. You have struggled to defend yourself, but the wounds on your body may heal, while those in your heart leave deep scars.
Empathy stirred within, making it impossible to blame him further. With you, the victim, vouching for him, the Sect Leader had no choice but to let the matter drop. After all, this person was not even a Tang Clan disciple and couldn't be punished according to their rules. With a wave of his sleeve, he turned and entered the inner chamber to rest.
You trusted him as faithfully as you had once hoped a hero would, extending kindness and generosity to him. Little did you know that on the surface he thanked you politely, but in his heart, he secretly laughed at you, seeing you as an easy mark for fools.
Who is this Chao He then? In the Jianghu, he goes by the nickname Zang Hong Cia. He doesn't deceive clever people; he only tricks people like you who are too kind.
He didn't care about how his actions would tarnish the last vestiges of goodness in the world, making benevolent people no longer trust others easily. He just took pleasure in it, outwardly agreeing and nodding, while inwardly hoping you, this kind but foolish pig, would die soon and not be reborn.

Bring the person to the Center Heart Hall and respectfully request that the Sect Leader conduct a personal review. On the side, Second Senior Brother, the Deputy Execution Officer, will assist.
Even if he were as cold as Second Senior Brother, upon seeing this person, he could not help but be surprised and approached to probe further, only to feel even more alarmed. Because this person was not merely disguised; they truly looked like that.
In fact, when the two of them stand together and look closely, they are clearly not the same person. His facial features are quite different from yours. He merely relies on others being too afraid to scrutinize him closely, so he mimics your outfit and hairstyle deliberately. When out in public, he keeps shouting I am Zhao Huo and I am the Ugly Xia of Tang Clan, which tricks those who have never met them or only know them superficially into believing him.
Upon meeting the Sect Leader's face, he immediately fell to his knees, sobbing loudly and claiming himself to be a victim as well.
He did not know that the one he was bowing to was a fake Tang Clan; selling counterfeit medicine was also instigated by his senior brothers; riding the horse and injuring someone was not something he willingly chose; rather, he was forcefully put on the horseback, and at that time, he was extremely frightened. Claiming to be the Wuxia of the Tang Clan was because he admired you; as for calling himself Sect Leader, it was merely conjecture by others. He had merely approached to speak, but was immediately labeled as a pervert.

A large crowd gathered around the person on the training ground. You recognized their face, and it struck you like a bolt from the blue‑this man's appearance bore a striking resemblance to yours. This was the infamous fake Zhao Huo, who had been impersonating you in Guangzhou, swindling people with counterfeit medicines. Now, he had gone so far as to steal money from a blind beggar's bowl. Caught red‑handed by the Beggar Sect, he attempted to frame you. However, Fan Xiaotian, with his sharp sense of smell, detected the pungent, mixed odor on the fake's body, realizing he hadn't bathed in days. This contrasted sharply with the subtle herbal fragrance that always lingered on you. Fan immediately declared him a fraud, sent dogs to attack, gathered the beggars to surround and beat him, and tied him up in five‑pointed binding before handing him over to the Tang Clan to claim a reward.

A crowd gathered around the person on the ground in the training arena. As you caught a glimpse of their face, it struck you like a bolt from the blue‑this man, by appearance alone, bore a striking resemblance to you. This was the infamous fake Zhao Huo, the one who had been impersonating you in Guangzhou, swindling people with counterfeit medicine. Now, he had gone so far as to target a blind beggar, stealing money from their bowl. Caught red‑handed by the Beggar Sect, he was beaten and mocked, then tied up in five‑point restraint and handed over to the Tang Clan for a reward.

\nOn this particular day, you were just about to rest when Fan Xiaotian suddenly burst into your disciple's room, startling you so much that you jumped. You thought that no matter how good your relationship was with him, he had no reason to suddenly barge into someone else's sect without warning. Moreover, you were in the middle of taking off your pants to change clothes for a nap.

\nOn this day, you were just about to rest when suddenly a beggar blundered into your apprentice room. You jumped in surprise. You thought that no matter how close the Tang Clan and Beggar Sect might be, it made no sense for him to barge into someone else's sect without warning like this, especially since you were in the middle of getting undressed to take a nap.

On this day, you were just about to rest when suddenly someone announced that Song Bei, Sir Official, had come to visit.
You stepped out to see that Song Guan wasn't the only official there; several more officials had arrived as well. This made you uneasy, wondering if you had done something wrong. However, instead of scolding you, Song Guan asked some strange and inexplicable questions. He inquired about your movements one moment, then whether you sold medicine the next, and even asked if you were married.

You encountered Shangguan Ying, who spread her hand out and demanded money from you.

The person who masqueraded as you likely feels rather pleased with himself after taking the money, but he vastly underestimates Lady Shangguan Xiao. Since there were no casualties, this matter could be trivial or serious. What really matters is that you, an insignificant person, are the one who gets wronged.
Chao He was certain that no one would step forward for him. He planned to hide for a few days to ride out the storm and then reappear as if nothing had happened when everyone had calmed down. Even if someone didn't probe too deeply, he could just cry and slap himself; could anyone really demand his life over this?
His prediction was actually not far off. Everyone was afraid of trouble, so as long as they stubbornly refused to confess, the Tang Clan couldn't force a confession out of them.
According to the Tang Clan's code of conduct, they indeed cannot torture someone into confessing. Without iron‑clad evidence, the official in charge of torturing would be at a loss what to do.
Fortunately, he had died his own death by acting on his self‑aggrandizement and ignoring the orders. It was only because of Second Senior Brother that he could be lawfully taken back to the mountain under these circumstances.
Cao He thought that by blending into the city, if Tang Clan tried to force a confrontation, he could roll around on the ground crying and make a fuss, drawing the attention of neighbors to mock him. In front of everyone, Handsome Saber broke Cao He's arms and legs using a dislocation technique, then hired someone with Coin to bind and carry him back up the mountain.
Chao He's adopted mother, Tang Xiaolou, heard the bad news and, leaving her own business, hurriedly tried to intercept him. However, no matter how she spoke, Second Senior Brother was neither convinced nor moved. She followed him all the way up the mountain and entered Zhengxin Hall, where she complained to the Sect Leader about the situation.
She wept and cried, accusing you and Second Senior Brother of being ruthless and domineering, defiling her adopted son. She begged the Sect Leader to make a decision and revoke your and Second Senior Brother's martial arts skills, expelling them from the sect.
Can one truly say that the Sect Leader is not wise and perceptive? How could they then be trusted?
The Breaker Sect admitted Chao He into the sect's walls out of consideration for their fellow disciples and would certainly not tolerate her misinterpreting right from wrong.
But he was too emotional about his old bonds. Thinking of the events from past years, he ultimately couldn't bring himself to be so harsh.
Only Chao He, in his own stead as the culprit, has undergone this, with the Sect Leader's dignity requesting punishment from the Palm Leader.
Tang Xiaolou had always favored people over principles and was the epitome of partiality. Without any offspring, she adopted this sweet‑tongued dry son, hoping he would one day take care of her in her old age. She spoiled him dearly. Yet, how could Sect Leader be any different from her old‑year comrade‑in‑arms, someone who had grown up alongside her?
Others tried to advise her with proper reasoning, but she only dismissed it as mere wind. It wasn't until the Sect Leader got hurt because of her rebelliousness that she finally started to wake up.
Leaving the Correct Heart Hall, I see Chao He with tears and snot streaming down his face. As soon as he got his limbs back, he asked if she had expelled both me and Second Senior Brother from the Tang Clan. Instantly, I was fuming and slapped him across the face.
She was very compassionate towards him and couldn't help feeling heartache as he began to cry again. Gently consoling him, she led him down the mountain, but secretly made up her mind that this would be the last time.
That Chao He, as the instigator who managed to escape unscathed in the end, felt a sense of guilt compared to Beggar Sect's Li Fugui and Songshan's Fu Yun. They settled in the outer fortress and helped repair all the damaged and destroyed objects from the destruction and looting that had taken place.

Fortunately, Third Senior Brother is reasonable; upon thinking about it, he realized something was amiss. Committing the crime and deliberately leaving a name‑this method sounds familiar. Could it be that the habitual offender forgot he's in Shu and wants to repeat the same trick, framing you?
The blame is directed at you, you feel an unbearable sense of injustice, enduring all sorts of suffering, always trying to be a good person, yet this is the consequence?

The blame is directed at you, and you feel utterly wronged. If you had done something wrong, that would be one thing, but you haven't gained any benefit and are still being unjustly accused. How can this be acceptable?

When it came to holding the perpetrators responsible for the accident at that time, both of the culprits looked uncomfortable and were momentarily at a loss for words.
At the time, it was true that a monk and a beggar were fighting over a pancake. However, Master Fu Yun's attempt to snatch Li Fugui's pancake had a deeper meaning.
Not a case of bullying, but rather an opportunity to cleanse the Beggar Sect of its tarnished reputation, so that neighbors and passersby can see for themselves: The heroes of the Beggar Sect are still hungry and destitute, but they strictly adhere to benevolence and righteousness, and refuse to bully the people with their strength.
What could have been a beautiful story was deliberately stirred up by malicious individuals for their own purposes.
With Chao He's actions, the monks of Songshan were harshly criticized for the evil deeds of the Beggar Sect; accusations against the members of the Beggar Sect were also levelled at the disciples of Songshan. This ultimately led to a great disaster.
This person tends to act cowardly in emergencies, but as soon as he has no involvement, he immediately becomes arrogant. In reality, he provoked the two sides to fight without considering any consequences at all. His motivation is truly shallow; he only did it because he was annoyed with you and wanted to ruin your reputation.
For this, he doesn't care how many people die; after all, in the end, it will be your fault when they investigate. So, even before Lord Yan, he would deny any connection to these deaths and blame you for everything.

You intervened without permission, so the other party really does put aside their grievances and unite to fight against your Tang Clan.\nThird Senior Brother was already at a loss on how to conclude the situation when suddenly he heard that someone was setting fire. This only made him more panicked and desperate.\nFortunately, all three parties are people of righteous valor. Upon seeing the common people in danger, they immediately transformed swords into plowshares and worked together to put out the fire.
You died in the chaotic battle and became the sole casualty.

You can only grit your teeth and risk being killed by your fellow disciples to stand on the opposing side.
However, you ignored what he said and joined your fellow students and brothers‑in‑arms in hatred against him.
I can only entrust you to persuade our own people, while they go to argue with the root cause of the incident.
Third Senior Brother couldn't control the situation at all.

Your Tang Clan's method is to Fight Their Mother.\nPeople tend to argue among themselves when they have too much idle time, but they unite in the face of natural disasters.\nTo reconcile the conflict between the Disciples of the Beggar Sect and the monks of Songshan Temple, the easiest way is to redirect this conflict, and for this, the Tang Clan is unwavering in their commitment to becoming natural disasters.
Mediating disputes is the Nangong Clan's specialty, but Lu Weng approached the Tang Clan instead. That's great; the Tang Clan also has their own methods of mediating disputes.
Mediating disputes and being a peacemaker are the Nangong family's duty. Yet Lu Weng approached the Tang Clan, and no matter how you think about it, you feel uneasy.

Upon hearing that Third Senior Brother said there was chaos at the outer fortress and that Lu Weng had come up the mountain for help, I only then found out.\nMuch like most cases in the Jianghu, the causes are typically trivial and infuriatingly small. Even Daoists and monks cannot remain immune to such base instincts.\nAfter all, this time it's monks and Beggar Sect disciples competing for alms, and the stakes are not just a matter of face but also a matter of food.

Second Senior Brother is not as rigidly conventional as Third Senior Brother; one can easily guess where the trouble began.\nHe ordered you to bring the quilts and reside in the Furnace Room to tend the fire for him. Even if Second Senior Brother finds you displeasing, as the Chief of Punishments, they remain impartial and unyielding. Unlike Third Senior Brother, who clings to conventions, they understand where trouble arises and have no energy to waste on someone as insignificant as you.

I just didn't expect you to be lying at home when the troubles still wouldn't spare you. When the fellow brothers returned from below the mountain, they all had strange looks on their faces when they saw you. It was Third Senior Brother who told us that there was a fight between the Songshan and Beggar Sect. Meanwhile, another disciple will be dispatched to summon Chao He up the mountain for questioning.

The senior brother, who had caught the constables, entered the room to find you sleeping. Just as he was about to scold you, he immediately thought of how busy you've been lately, with no moment to rest. You still wanted to pretend you hadn't heard, so the senior brother rushed into the room, beat you up, and dragged you out.

After that, Ye Yunzhao sat in the forge holding his sword and stayed awake through the night. You opened the window to check on him, finding him motionless as if deeply asleep, but in reality, he did not dare to truly fall asleep for a moment.
Just as you do not trust him, he does not trust you.
The next morning, he went to the mountains to split bamboo and built a simple bamboo shelter, then went to pick up his younger sister Yunshang to live with him.
However, after being unfeelingly rejected by her brother, Ye Yunshang now enjoys great favor and lives in luxury, with no desire to go back to sharing a humble cottage with them.

After that, Ye Yunzhao sat holding his sword in the smithy and stayed awake through the night, seeming to be deeply asleep. However, you looked out the window and saw him still and motionless; he was actually keeping himself awake for the entire time.\nJust as you don't trust him, he doesn't trust you.

Though I can't say all my suspicions have vanished, it's only polite to let him stay in my room for the night.

Ye Yunzhao also realized the difficulty of this matter and volunteered to stay overnight in the forge. The next morning, he would move into the outer fortress.

The Sect Leader stepped back and had a deep discussion with the Ye family siblings.

Call in the little junior sister as well; she's around the same age as Ye Yunshang, and it's meant to have them keep each other company.

Ye Yunzhao didn't have such good luck. The more his reputation grew, the tenser his fellow Tang Clan brothers and sisters became, fearing that he might be killed in his sleep by a single sword stroke.

The Sect Leader dismissed the people on either side and had a deep conversation with the Ye family siblings.\nWith a heart to persuade Ye Yunzhao to stay, he heard that the young man seemed intent on leaving. Ye Yunzhao and Ye Yunshang, as siblings, had never encountered someone who handled matters with such decisive resolve. Even Little Junior Sister was summoned together. As for you, your task is to clean up the aftermath by cooking and preparing meals.

The Sect Leader immediately summoned Ye Yunzhao. Seeing him bow and press his palms together in respect, the attitude was genuinely reverent. The Sect Leader nodded slightly and first asked about his background. Ye Yunzhao did not hide anything and admitted that according to family tradition, his great‑great‑grandfather indeed served under the military governor Yue Yun, the Marquis of Wukang, with the Hearcloud Sword as proof.
Although the Sect Leader is resentful of the corruption and oppression by the court, he greatly respects loyal ministers and filial sons. He believes that Ye family ancestors followed Yue Yun Gong, earning great trust and being granted the treasure sword Tingyun, which indicates that they must have achieved much through hard work and remained faithful to their duties.
Determined to protect this brother‑sister pair, he made an exception and stepped in as a peacemaker, aiming to resolve their dispute.
Ye Yunzhao, backed by the Sect Leader's support, dared to speak in front of everyone. Without much ado, he was met with a chorus of skeptical voices. Seeing this, the Sect Leader responded calmly with a single word: Anyone who dares to speak out will have their mouth torn shut.
In the vast training ground, it fell silent instantly. They couldn't help but think simultaneously,: Is there really a mediator so vicious in the world?
Ye Yunzhao's willpower surged as he vented his pent‑up frustration. He imagined the Martial Valor King, who devoted himself to his country and longed to spend all his money on grain, armor, and horses; where would he ever hoard any wealth?
Even if the people of Henan province welcomed them with incense pots along the streets, how many assets could the people from areas that had been plundered by the Jurchens be able to offer?
The King Wu Mu died eighty years ago. Even if the legends are true and there are treasures, the Yue Family is not extinct; why haven't they taken them out to use yet?
When it comes to the Red Reed King, Mr. Zeng Wen, Chang Xian and Zhang Chengxuan, which one of them is not a capable commander worthy of important responsibilities? As for the notion of tattoos, it is pure speculation with no basis at all. One can only wonder where such rumors originate.
He had spoken with sincere and earnest honesty, too.
But how many of those present are willing to listen? Those who don't know him personally can simply have their greedy and suspicious hearts at ease. The ones who used to call each other brothers and sisters every day, now pressing on so desperately‑this is a bit too heart‑chilling.
Ye Yunzhao spoke with every word ringing clear and firm, making logical sense that left everyone in the room looking at each other.
However, after a moment of silence, Shen Ji still did not give up, citing national interests as the reason and insisting on further investigation. I just want to have some formal justification for this. Why not sacrifice the reputation of a mere woman? After all, she's not my own sister, so damaging her reputation doesn't really hurt me. At worst, we can all apologize and make amends later, and find someone to marry her off.
Ye Yunzhao found himself in a predicament much like a scholar facing an army‑logic could not be effectively used. He was both angry and embarrassed. Even so, the monk did not press the matter. The young novice steadied himself and still admitted that he was a disciple of Songshan in Henan. To his surprise, the Sect Leader's expression softened considerably. He then asked about the novice's Zen Master, which immediately changed the leader's demeanor to one of pleasant smiles, quite unlike how he had been moments ago.
The old and young immediately began chatting as if they were peers, discussing the circumstances leading up to matters. Such a world‑renowned hero could not withstand schemes and calculations.
That young monk has taken refuge in the Songshan Mountain in Henan Province and feels a deep gratitude towards Yue Fei. He wants to contribute to the counties of Henan by assisting them. Even if such treasures were indeed given to the court, it would only result in more mansions for the officials, more fancy horses, and more pretty concubines for them.
After finishing his questions, they allowed the monk to leave. Everyone breathed a sigh of relief upon seeing the monk return unharmed.

The crowd chattered for a while but could not agree on anyone to propose.

Upon arrival, he immediately wanted to assert himself by creating an impression of dominance. He swung his large saber with a fierce and menacing movement, shouting, You rascals, what are you worth? Do you think you can rebel against the authorities? And then he went straight to hell.
Today, the officials from the government who came are not just him. Anyone with a bit of experience knows that the Tang Clan is a thorn in the side of the court. This constable not only spoke maliciously but also threatened the sect leader with a blade, which is getting exactly what he deserved.
Let another person step forward to speak. This time, no one dared to raise their hand. The Sect Leader had no patience left and simply pointed at a burly‑eyed boy from the Beggar Sect who happened to be nearby.
Li Fugui comes from the Beggar Sect. He has a simple and honest look on his face and immediately knelt down upon meeting him, thinking that he must be showing such a grand courtesy out of fear. Only you would unconditionally choose her, encourage her, and select her as the First Palm Dispatched Lady despite nobody else looking favorably upon her.
To Yu Xiaozhu, you are the Head of the Clan and her ultimate destination. If you don't want her either, the rest of her life will be nothing to celebrate.
Fortunately, she's very easy to deceive. As long as the lies are for her sake, she'll believe them without hesitation.
Having you all the way to the end is better than a long and lonely life ahead.

Suddenly a disciple came to report that someone was being carried up the mountain in a sedan chair. At first, we thought it was the Wulin Alliance making a sudden move, but it turns out it's actually the Kongtong Guardian.

But the Wulin Alliance is narrow‑minded and believes that Kongtong fabricated military intelligence as a delaying tactic.

Xiao Mei and you are only nominally together for now. Once you're gone, she still has her whole life ahead, and it's not necessarily about staying with you.
But she is obsessively devoted to you in a almost pathological way. All along, her ability to behave normally and talk to you civilly has already been an effort in itself.
Since you're going to die today anyway, she doesn't have to pretend to be a virtuous person anymore.
Startling proclamation: While you're alive, I can't claim your physical body for myself. But now that you are dead, her remains should be returned to her. When cremated into ashes, we can brew tea with them‑blending perfectly together, ensuring eternal separation.

You were pleasantly surprised to see Xiao Mei upon first sight. Upon asking, you learned that a major event had occurred at Kongtong since your last meeting, which is why you couldn't immediately rush to Tang Clan's aid, for this very reason.

The military intelligence was transmitted through the official relay system over eight hundred li in urgent haste, but alas, as the saying goes, a step ahead of evil is far, and the Joyful Teachings sect had been hidden in Western Shu for years, infiltrating various states long ago. While they were speaking, a strange whirlwind swept across the ground. You executed a backflip to take down the opponent, narrowly avoiding breaking Xiao Mei's arm.

Beating her won't ease your anger; you need to pacify her wrath by treating her to delicious food and drinks every day, cherishing her like a precious gem. You must beg for her forgiveness for a hundred days before she will forgive you.\nSo you can't treat today as your day of death.

Not only do you refuse to apologize, but you also try to act deep and philosophical, emulating the roving and sentimental wanderer of the world.\nYe Yunshang doesn't buy into your tactics. Otherwise, who will listen to her complaints and grievances?

She made you bend over and pull a staff from the jacket to beat you with it.\nWho let this ugly fellow talk his way into stealing her heart and go after others as well? Even Third Senior Brother thinks you deserve to get beaten for it.
Knowing you won't return, I remain obsessed, willing to risk my prime youth, distilling my tears into wine to await you.

Ye Yunshang refused to leave, alive or dead, clinging to the pillar of Zhengxin Hall without letting go, until those who advised her had all left. Only then did she step out, looking at the Third Senior Brother and at you, wanting to imprint your appearances in her heart.

\nThere's no such thing as a completely secret matter. You toyed with the feelings of these young women, and it has finally come to light. Poor fellow, the Wulin Alliance will attack the mountain tomorrow, but you'll have to die today.

Sect Master Zou Zhidong sighed long and short as Tang Fang delivered his business card at the foot of the mountain. Since the grand assembly at Fengyu Mountain, Zhuo Sect Master has been gloomy and unhappy every day.
