Mastered under Jinxiang Palace, the ingenious and exquisite swordswoman. Walking in her father's footsteps with a solemn step, she yearns to fulfill her father's aspirations by roaming the four quarters as a wanderer of justice. Despite this, due to her naivety regarding worldly affairs, she is surprisingly prone to falling victim to deceit.

On the day her family was destroyed and she lost everything, the young Yunshang was struck by a martial artist sent by the Imperial Court. Her dantian shattered, her meridians severed; it seemed she could not survive. Later, after enduring countless hardships, she barely managed to preserve her life, entering the Diancang sect as an apprentice. Though she appeared innocent and carefree, she was always wary and cautious, even of the master who saved her life. It wasn't until you and Moling appeared that things changed. She bitterly regretted that, being a woman, she could never hope to marry Moling in this lifetime. But at least she could settle for second best‑marrying you. Although you are ugly, she would have preferred death rather than consent to such a union; who knew that you were so determined and persistent, chasing her even into hell? Having been treated with such care and affection, can anyone in the world remain untouched by such devotion? In any case, she could not accept it.

They carry a significant secret. The ancestor of the Ye siblings was one of the capable generals under Yue Yun, the son of the renowned anti‑Jin general, King Wu Mu. It is said that Emperor Gaozong issued twelve imperial edicts in a row, but Yue Fei, loyal and righteous, willingly met his death, lamenting that the great cause against the Jin had not been completed. If military power were to be seized by treacherous individuals, the Song Dynasty would be powerless to turn the tide. Therefore, the main force of the Yue Clan army was dispersed, and treasures were hidden in the mountains. Iron military tokens were cast and entrusted to the eldest son, Yue Yun, in hopes that in the future, they could use the tokens to command the old troops and continue the mission of protecting the nation. Unexpectedly, Yue Yun died before his father, and in a moment of crisis, he entrusted the military tokens to a subordinate, instructing them to hide in Jianghu and wait for the descendants of Wu Mu to come for them. That subordinate then concealed their identity, living in seclusion in the mountains, and has since guarded the military tokens through generations. When chaos erupted in Baifeng Cave, the Ye family was implicated and suffered the wrath of the current emperor, leading to a tragic massacre of their clan, leaving the Ye siblings orphaned.

I wondered why I came down the mountain with my elder brother, but we were captured by Diancang Mountain's men. In the Jianghu, those who covet are not few, so it's necessary to hide our movements. Choosing to enjoy no‑worry days instead, we decided to wander freely across the land regardless. The journey was arduous, increasing her chances of falling ill with fever more frequently. Whenever she became drowsy, holding onto my elder brother's robe would allow her to sleep soundly. Having a brother is enough; I don't need anything else. To survive like this, relying on each other, just as before...

Ye Yunzhao's twin sister, the ill beauty I See and Pity. Born frail, she often falls ill and lies bedridden with fever, but fortunately her nature is optimistic, so she doesn't mind it too much. She likes to act coy, and both Diancang Upper and Lower Sects dote on her, almost able to summon wind and rain. Although she practices the Diancang martial arts Heart Method under her brother's urging, limited by her physical condition, even if she memorizes everything perfectly, she makes little progress. She would pant even from walking a bit faster, let alone wielding blades or swords. She doesn't have any particular hobbies, but is filled with curiosity about the world below. Hating to endure hardships and hate taking medicine, she will vomit if force‑fed, and after vomiting, she will mock people with a smug expression as though enjoying their misfortune.

Ye Yunzhao's twin sister. Even in the sweltering summer, she never parted with her fox‑fur cloak. Though she was a mischievous and playful beautiful girl, she would always fall ill after half a day of causing trouble.
Rui Xing
Rui Xing

Originally, he was more rebellious and unyielding, with a touch of recklessness. He believed his sword techniques had reached perfection; in the entire world, there was no one who could match him. Eager to make a name for himself, he was about to venture out from the mountains when his cousin called him to the Southern Meadow of Apricot Blossoms in Nanyang. There, he was confined for three whole months using an odd gate array formation. He cried out to heaven and earth but no one answered; even trying to escape by flying or digging underground did not work, as he was trapped under Fairy Apricot's Five‑Finger Mountain. After being released, he had lost several pounds and became humble and kind. At the same time, he understood that she was a dangerous person he could not interfere with. He was also ordered not to entice Wei Ju, which made him feel very wronged.

At a young age, they possessed an extraordinary level of martial arts skill for some unknown reason. They claimed to come from the Guyun Mountain Sect, yet no one had ever heard of this obscure minor sect. Filled with aspirations for the Jianghu, they carried a sword and traveled far and wide, meddling in other people's affairs and championing the underdog. Their demeanor was humble yet emotionally committed, making them extremely popular among everyone they met across various factions. Since coming down from the mountain, many young misses had been drawn to him, but his favored ones were all formidable opponents, thus leaving him with numerous setbacks.

A young swordsman making his debut. Handsome and elegant, a straightforward gentleman, he conducts himself with worldliness yet harbors boundless heroism within. Wielding his sword to right wrongs and settle grievances, he always appears at critical moments.

One of Rui Sheng's red‑haired confidants, the holy lady of the Miaojiang Wu Ling sect. Even in her mother's womb, she was designated as the wife of the dragon by a village witch. Along with three or four friends, Rui Sheng entered the Miaojiang region, breached the Five Immortals Array, wielded a sword to slash at a giant snake, and exposed the plot of Golden Toad Mother Lady and Silver Snake Young Lord. In the end, she became the object of admiration as the hero rescued the beauty. She constantly feuded with her other red‑haired confidants day in and day out, but despite being a backstabber with a bad mouth, she was kind at heart and could not bring herself to use magic to harm others, so she ended up suffering all her life in silence.

One of Rui Sheng's beautiful confidants, the Holy Maiden of the Witch Spirit Sect from Miaojiang. Even while still in their mother's womb, they were foretold by the clan's witch to be the wife of a dragon. Rui Sheng, along with a few close friends, ventured into Miaojiang, broke through the Five Immortals Array, wielded their sword to slay a giant serpent, and uncovered the schemes of the Golden Toad Lady and the Silver Serpent Young Lord, delighting in the heroic rescue of the damsel in distress.

Before his father joined the Beggar Sect, he had held official rank and position. He only had one son, Li Fugui, whom he doted on immensely. Li Fugui was uneducated but showed no lack of mischief; by the age of five, he would even pull up a girl's skirt. Later, after Thousand Gold Hermit disbursed his family wealth and joined the Beggar Sect, Li Fugui remained arrogant and willful, relying on his father's influence to act with impunity. It wasn't until Wang Erzhuang took over from Thousand Gold Hermit and became the sect leader that there was no one to shield Li Fugui. Only then did he begin to rein in his arrogance, changing his name and acknowledging Wang Erzhuang as his father, with the intention of assassinating him. Unbeknownst to Li Fugui, Wang Erzhuang had been watching all this carefully. He believed that such a boy could endure hardships and was worth training. However, Li Fugui couldn't hold back for long; he attempted the assassination on the same night he became his father's son, but of course, the attempt failed miserably. The punishment was inevitable, but it wasn't physical abuse or execution; instead, Wang Erzhuang forced him to study and train in martial arts, tormenting both his mind and body.

A new rising star in the Beggar Sect, despite being a beggar, he was named Fugui. Being both an orphan of the Elder Thousand Elders from the old faction and an adopted son of Wang Erzhuang, the leader and boss of the new faction of the Beggar Sect, he stutters when speaking, yet isn't unintelligent.

Jie Wuchen, although a member of the righteous sect, was known for his competitive and martial spirit. He would often seek out renowned experts to challenge, which had led to many setbacks. His unique master technique, Wind Thunder Divine Foot, is a combination of his family's Wind God Step and Emei's ultimate art Thunder God Foot. When deployed, it allows him to kick while borrowing force, launching him high into the air with deadly precision. They use this technique to gain momentum from their opponent's force, sending themselves soaring through the air with pinpoint accuracy. The alias Wind God was given to him for five taels of silver by a friend; otherwise, he wouldn't have such a fearsome nickname.

The contemporary famous young master of the Emei Sect, known as the Wind God, is renowned in the Jianghu alongside the Tang Clan's flying hero, Tang Buyi. This Emei master excels in leg techniques and claims to be a formidable rival to your senior apprentice brother. They are quite bothersome, often getting into fights upon meeting, but there are also tales of them adventuring together in the Jianghu.

They once captured a young girl who had been imprisoned in a cellar as a forbidden delicacy. In her escape, she killed her captor in self‑defense. Out of pity, they let the innocent perpetrator go, but this act was seized upon by their brother's political enemies, who reported them to the Dali Temple. Song Bei argued sternly, The penal code has been established for two hundred years, and the customs of the people have changed. It is inappropriate to rigidly adhere to old rules. Moreover, the law was created by our ancestors, who, being high in the halls of power, do not understand the feelings of the people and must have overlooked certain aspects, which could lead to injustice and harm to the world. Where the law does not align with reason, I act with compassion and have a clear conscience. However, the defense failed, and Song Bei was punished with a six‑month salary reduction and confined to their residence. Fortunately, their brother Song Ci was active in the court, and with petitions from the common people, the Dali Temple eventually rescinded the order and granted them a special pardon.

Although officially appointed as an Anzhi Bao'an Lang, which is a seventh‑rank position, the title of carrying a blade in front of the emperor means that even a first‑rank official cannot insult them at will. They are, after all, the emperor's blade, and they take pride in that. Unless it is the emperor, they maintain a demeanor that is neither arrogant nor servile, which reflects both the expectations of the imperial family and the courage they have forged in the Jianghu. If corrupt officials are discovered, even the prince dares to arrest them. Conversely, they are also quite compassionate; they can recite the laws of Song by heart, but when faced with situations that the law cannot accommodate, they often turn a blind eye or plead for leniency.

Grand Captains of the Great Song, granted with the Imperial Silver Fish Bag and assigned a personal knife by the court. Acting as the chief commander for all law enforcement across the land, they have the authority to apprehend suspects beyond the state borders. Roaming through the Jianghu, they are considered somewhat part of the Wulin.

It was common for female admirers to feign being tormented by demons in order to catch a glimpse of his handsome face, pretending to seek his magical help at Qingcheng. Shentu Long, fully aware that it was a ruse, never exposed their deception out of consideration for their feelings. The Taoist priests of Qingcheng took it upon themselves to exorcise demons and eliminate evil, but Shentu Long did not believe in the existence of such creatures. If there were truly anything in the world that could be deemed evil, it would be humanity itself.

Shentu Long, known as Yicen Daozi, of the Qingcheng Sect. Though young in age, he holds a high rank due to his seniority. He is a closed‑door disciple of the previous Qingcheng Sect Master. With a refined and handsome appearance, he is easygoing and scholarly. When not practicing Taoist cultivation techniques, he often wanders around the mountains, rarely getting involved with Jianghu affairs. He seldom argues with others, but during the monthly examinations within the Qingcheng Sect, his martial arts skills are on full display. Despite this, his reputation still managed to spread quietly.

They were straightforward, honest, and earnest in their pursuit of immortality, following the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch in their cultivation. They felt deeply ashamed that, after years of training, they still could not breathe fire. Although they had not succeeded in cultivating immortal techniques, they were actually a person of great fortune and destiny. By chance, they learned the Wind Blade and Fire Sword, which made their master envious. Thus, under the pretext that to break through to the Great Ascension stage, one must accumulate merit, and the fastest way to accumulate merit is to go to the battlefield to save the nation, they were deceived into the Song‑Jin battlefield to face death. However, they remained on the battlefield and did not die; instead, they earned the trust of the officials and soldiers, being honored as the General of Dao Techniques, with remarkable military achievements, even receiving special treatment from General Zhao Fang, the defending general of Xiangyang.

Kongtong Sect·Feitian Gate Palm Master Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch's senior disciple. Also known as the famed 'Way of Dao Military General' on the Xiangyang battlefield, undefeated in a hundred battles, revered by Song people and civilians, feared by Jin troops.

Wang Chunxiao, whose ancestral lineage consisted of military officials, benefited from their legacy and was granted the title of Dingyuan Lang. However, he was cultured and refined, preferring poetry and chess over martial prowess. Although he had read military texts, the thought of going to battle to defend his homeland made him tremble. It wasn't until he met Nangong Yuan and encountered Su Yingxiang that he reluctantly ventured into the Jianghu to win the favor of the beauty. In every aspect, he excelled beyond Nangong Yuan, but in Su Yingxiang's eyes, she only favored Nangong Yuan. This left Wang Chunxiao heartbroken, weeping and despondent, even running to Donglin Temple in tears, contemplating shaving his head to become a monk. It was there that he encountered an opportunity that would change his life. He became a disciple of Master Chunmian, intending to learn Buddhism, but Master Chunmian insisted on forcing him to practice martial arts. It was only much later that Wang Chunxiao learned that his master was the renowned Red Peng Wang, the Martial Overlord of the Eastern Thirteen States.

Their gaze is lazy, filled with a sense of defeat and negativity, with a fondness for fishing. They claim not to enjoy drinking, yet often end up thoroughly intoxicated. Wang Erzhuang is the key figure in the Beggar Sect's transformation from darkness to light. Since taking command, they have vigorously promoted chivalry, reigniting hope in the eyes of young disciples of the Beggar Sect, encouraging them to believe that even when mired in filth, they can emerge untainted. As long as one harbors a sense of chivalry, even in humble attire, they can take pride; after all, the most incorruptible officials are those with empty sleeves. The new faction has risen, sweeping away the Beggar Sect's past vices, acting with integrity and no longer engaging in petty thefts, eager to uphold justice. The old faction still holds significant power, simultaneously criticizing the new faction for being unorthodox and claiming to be noble while benefiting from the good name earned by the new faction.

The leader of the Beggar Sect, the number one sect in the world, took office with decisive action, promoting new disciples while sidelining the old‑school elders. They used the spirit of chivalry to deceive the sect's members into reclaiming their dignity, making them believe that being a beggar was a choice.

Gifted with sharp intellect and formidable eloquence, he frequently traversed between Emei and Kongtong, promoting Buddhism while soliciting donations to construct temples on Songshan. He treated good people with respect but was stern with those who were obstinate. His attitude toward you depended on your character; he would inevitably chatter, though the difference lay in whether his words irritated you or not.
The young disciple of the Songshan Sect traveled throughout Great Song to propagate Buddhism and raise funds for the restoration of the dilapidated Songshan Temple.

In their youth, they had successively taken Ma Yu and Liu Chuxuan as teachers, but were caught by their parents and locked in the woodshed. Seeing their urgent desire to seek the Dao, their family finally let them go.

Quanzhen Qinghezi Yin Zhiping was the favored disciple of Qiu Chuji, the Quanzhen School's 'Supreme Master Under Heaven.' During his revered teacher's travels, Yin Zhiping managed Mount Zhongnan's Quanmen Monastery and there were whispers that he might succeed to the position of Grand Master in the near future.

The moment Nangong Qian laid eyes on the grand five‑court residence of the Nangong family, his eyes sparkled. The clothes these people wore were so fine; some even had gold threads on them. It seemed that princes and young lords were no different. His father was more dashing and formidable than he imagined, someone even officials would greet respectfully. His brother was well‑versed and courteous; during their first meeting, he even offered Qian a sweet treat. He actually became part of their family, thinking good times were ahead. However, it wasn't like that at all. The patriarch treated everyone kindly except for him and his mother, whose disdain was obvious to everyone. As a result, the family members and servants grew increasingly contemptuous. After his mother passed away, no one protected him anymore, and he declined day by day, even being bullied by mere servants. Although living in the Nangong family wasn't worried about food or clothing, the Nangong household didn't even worry about feeding their dogs. The carefree child of old now walked with a timid gait, constantly reading people's expressions to get through each day.

In the early days of their memories, they followed their mother. At that time, they did not know what poverty was; life was simple and beautiful. They had good looks, were lively and intelligent, kind‑hearted, and loved by everyone. The children in the village all enjoyed playing with them. Back then, they were not called Nangong Qian; it seemed they had another nickname, which is now forgotten. One day, after playing and getting covered in mud, they curiously asked their mother, Why don't I have a father? Where did my father go? From that moment, their beautiful childhood came to an abrupt end.

The youngest son of the Nangong family. His birth was not what people had hoped for, and his mother was deeply loathed by Nangong Yuan. As a result, even Nangong Qian was not favored; though he is the second young lord, his treatment at home is no better than that of the servants.

Inspired by the story of the Chu King Wu Wang ending his life by suicide at the Wu River, he took it as a warning and believed that mere martial prowess was not enough to achieve anything. He asked, Has there ever been an emperor who relied solely on his own combat skills? Those who rely on brute strength are merely wasting their lives. Therefore, with all these matters, he only dabbled superficially. The Great Prince excelled in the Four Arts‑calligraphy, music, chess, and painting‑but did not pursue them deeply. His attitude toward learning was simply to get by, relying on his eloquence to cover up any shortcomings. He believed that his true challenge lay in knowing people well and making good use of their talents, mobilizing the strongest warriors and the most learned scholars. Although he possessed some talent and strategy, he could not escape the habits of a pampered young lord‑greedy for pleasure and fond of beauties. Together with three or five friends, he was known as one of the Four Young Masters of Flower City, frequenting brothels and courtesan quarters. If Shangguan Ying did not have a thin skin but a hard punch, they might have had problems even before their wedding.

Grown up hearing and seeing the ways of the world, and being both intelligent and quick‑witted, they adeptly utilized family assets and connections. They learned martial arts directly from their father and practiced calligraphy under guidance from a master. Their lifestyle was as luxurious as that of the nobility in Lin'an, despite lacking official titles or honors. Considering themselves above others, they often displayed a certain level of worldliness in their dealings. They had an engagement with Shangguan Ying, the only daughter of Shangguan Family, but their meetings were either arguments or physical confrontations.

The eldest legitimate son of the Nangong clan. He bears all the attention upon himself as the heir, continuing his family's legacy with a scholarly and graceful demeanor. Skilled in all four arts, he is not only widely known among the people of the Jianghu but also has connections within the circle of literati and refined scholars.

All began with a misunderstanding, yet the mistake proved grave and none was willing to back down. In the end, it was you who stepped in, turning swords into plowshares and broken mirrors back together, making all past grievances as fleeting clouds. Although Shi Gongyuan has now washed his hands of Tang Clan's affairs, retired with his beloved wife from Jianghu, he still harbors a debt to their family. Secretly vowing that should the Tang Clan ever face difficulties in the future, he cannot watch idly.

With the support of his virtuous wife, Shi Gongyuan gathered former bandits and started anew, founding the Flying Stone Gang. They specialized in renting out labor for heavy manual work and miscellaneous tasks, engaging in outsourcing businesses. While they did not discriminate in recruiting people based on their character, they strictly adhered to the gang rules, ensuring that none of them disturbed the peace or livelihood of the common folk. Shi Gongyuan himself underwent a transformation, becoming a righteous and benevolent person. The Flying Stone Gang rose to prominence rapidly, achieving hundreds of members within less than twenty years and being able to challenge the three major gangs in the Jianghu.

After the governor's daughter became the wife of the bandit leader, Shi Gongyuan's carefree life came to an end. No one knew that the delicate young lady was actually a fierce tigress, more formidable than the burly man himself. The poor bandit leader found himself under strict control of his wife. Under her gentle persuasion, he went to the yamen to plead for forgiveness, facing imprisonment and torture, believing he would surely die this time. However, it was his young wife who interceded and secured his release. The governor brought him into the inner hall, pardoned his past crimes, and ordered him to bow down, finally acknowledging him as a son‑in‑law.

Shi Gongyuan, in his youth, had once joined the military, serving as a minor soldier under General Bi Zaiyu. Later, he deserted and took refuge in Mount Maoshi in Maji State, becoming a mountain bandit. Shi Gongyuan lacked grand ambitions; he lived day by day, drinking and eating with his companions. He drunkenly lived life to the fullest, viewing violence as courage. His external skills were well‑developed, making him strong and muscular. This only made him more unrestrained. He even brazenly kidnapped a newly appointed magistrate during his walk and forcibly married the magistrate's daughter as his primary wife.

The Flying Stone Gang Master Shi was a robust and daring hero. Initially, he was a bandit operating in Maozhou. After getting married, he washed his hands in a Golden Basin, ceasing to disrupt the people's lives. Instead, he rented out manpower to handle rough work, and the Flying Stone Gang's reputation gradually spread far and wide, becoming a force that could challenge the three major gangs.

That battle left the Songshan monastery greatly weakened. The Abbot's cultivation was exhausted, without attachment, yet his faith in Buddhism grew stronger. His fellow monks were inspired by his dedication and returned to their original aspirations, abandoning martial arts and other minor skills for profound Buddhist teachings. Only he remained, restless from the lingering warmth of that battle. Unwilling to let go of his attachments, he resolutely stepped down as abbot and traveled far to the Mud Cult headquarters in Six Paths Canyon, where he sat alongside Heavenly King Che Xuanxuan to debate and spar with him. Surprisingly, this lifelong Buddhist found himself unable to dissuade a mortal, instead being enlightened by this ordinary person's insights into his own biases. Sitting for several days, he finally decided to return to secular life, though regretting that his hair was already balding in large patches. He recalled the 'Toujianke Zuan' he had read long ago and wove a cloak from eagle feathers collected over many years. The new martial artist Wanli Pengcheng began wandering Jianghu, completing his youthful journey.

Many years ago, someone slipped a legendary novel, 'The Record of the Hair‑Raisingly Bold,' into the Repository Chamber. The young monk Juekong stumbled upon it by chance and was deeply moved. He longed for the bold spirit depicted in the book and became obsessed with martial arts. Unfortunately, he had been ordained at Shaolin Temple since his youth and knew nothing about worldly affairs. All that he heard and witnessed were doctrines of abstaining from killing and distancing oneself from greed, anger, and delusion. Even if he wanted to venture into the world for a tour, it would be difficult for him to surpass himself. At such times of restlessness, he could only relieve his frustration by practicing a few fists. Although he lived outside the world, his heart lingered in this realm. He endured through several seasons, and even as the head monk of the Damao Hall, he could only find emptiness. It wasn't until the time when the Demon Sect, Supreme Bliss Sect, became rampant that the young hero Long Yuan rallied the heroes. Shaolin responded immediately to his call. Juekong was fortunate enough to be part of this event and gained a great reputation in that battle, impressing everyone with his skills as head monk of Damao Hall.

To gain fame and enter the world of the Jianghu, no matter how actively he moves around, the name of the Eagle does not spread far. He continues to wander between the borders of Song and Jin, sometimes being heard that he aids Chong in his cruelties, giving sermons to victorious Song soldiers after minor campaigns, which often annoys people. Although he is old, his actions are quite bloody‑minded. The heroes of Central Plains may not form alliances with him, but he is very popular among the people of both nations. He enjoys drinking, but his alcohol tolerance is rather poor.

He was once a figure in the tale, the head of the Dharma Academy at Songshan Temple, with his dharma name being Juekong. Juekong Zen Master possessed seven out of seventy‑two martial arts skills, and was particularly skilled in external skill Dragon Claw Hand. His martial prowess was no less than that of Senior Brother Abbot. Despite his high position and great virtue, he seldom walked among the Jianghu. Upon reaching the age of natural destiny, he resigned from his post as chief monk and journeyed far to Pengyang's Six Paths Canyon to challenge the Mud Cult's Heavenly King. After that, there was no trace of him. When he reappeared, he had already renounced his vows, taking on the name Eagle Man for himself.

A robust elderly man dressed in a cloak made of eagle feathers and broken straw raincoat. Despite his unusual appearance, his martial arts style is vast and profound, exuding an extraordinary demeanor, clearly indicating he is a master of his craft. It is unknown why, at this age, he remains unsung and unrecognized.

Her graceful name is Fan Siaoyan. Her mother named her in hopes that she would live a carefree life and always smile sweetly. Unfortunately, she encountered an evil beggar who specialized in the gruesome practice of harvesting organs from living victims. This man abducted the young girl, intending to turn her into a 'human dog.' Fortunately for her, she was born with extraordinary beauty, prompting him to take her as his concubine instead, keeping her hidden away in the beggars' den to amuse and toy with her until she grew stronger. Had it not been for the intervention of Gang Master Wang, this would have come to pass. Even so, being raised as a dog left no part of her body unscathed. Perhaps there is a haven in this world, even amidst constant border conflicts and night markets offering light and shelter; but there is nowhere that belongs to her. Not until your appearance. She trusts you and remains loyal to you alone. You are the only home she has.

The incident where he once attacked the Eight Bag Elders with poison had its reasons. He was a descendant of the Khitan Liao people who destroyed a nation a hundred years ago. Since his birth, all he could remember was following his parents as they wandered through Central Plains. Now those memories were already quite hazy. After his parents passed away, he was left only with an old dog named Ah Hua. Ah Hua had a discerning spirit; it would drive away mosquitoes and snakes to keep him safe when he was young, always by his side like a family member. One night, he woke up feeling cold and found that Ah Hua was gone. Instead, the elderly beggars were holding bowls of dog meat soup and sharing it among themselves. He felt lost and heartbroken for a long time before finally shedding tears. From that day on, he became an orphan with no one to care about or cherish.

In the Beggar Sect, he also stood out like a sore thumb. He had few close peers and could be persuaded by very few to do things. Since childhood, his rendition of Lianhua Luo was always poor, leading him to often fail at begging. Without the care of an elderly beggar named Uncle, he might have starved to death long ago. Perhaps because of this, he had always been willing to follow Uncle's instructions. In front of others, he acted like a wild dog, but by Uncle's side, he was very obedient. Although he didn't get along well with people, he seemed to have a fondness for small animals, often seen sharing hard‑won food with stray animals.

From the Beggar Sect, a rising new talent in recent years in the Jianghu. He believes in the survival of the fittest. The weak are destined to be oppressed, while only the strong can survive in this world. Don't underestimate him just because he is short; when it comes to fighting, he fights like a rabid dog, using every part of his body‑punches, claws, knees, elbows, and teeth. He is fearless, ruthless, and deadly. He learned a set of 'Dog‑beating Fist' from somewhere, the name crude but cleverly devised, emphasizing one word: 'ruthlessness.' Each move aims to finish the opponent off. Once, he followed an elderly Eight‑Bag Elder at midnight as he went to use the bathroom, brutally beat him until he was unconscious, breaking his limbs and pushing him into a latrine. Since then, even the long‑tenured Eight‑Bag Elders in the sect dared not act old‑fashioned or presumptuous in front of this man, for he is mad. Not only would he dare to fight anyone regardless of gender or age, but rumors have it that even Emperor of the Great Song might be within his reach.

A new rising star from the Beggar Sect of Jianghu. Known as 'Raging Dog,' don't underestimate his small stature; whenever he gets into a fight, it's all‑out war. Not only do outsiders fear him, but even members of the Beggar Sect dare not easily provoke this mad young man.

He is constantly probing you, holding high hopes for you while also waiting for your betrayal. When you reveal a greedy face, he will stab you with one sword and at the same time abandon his last shred of conscience, becoming an avenging demon to slaughter all enemies. However, it seems that your actions have disappointed his expectations; you are not a saint but merely more fixated on human emotions than treasure, thus making him believe that 'righteousness' does indeed exist in this world. The hidden decision to be selfish for once is beginning to make sense. You saved the life of his only relative and revived his heart, allowing him to no longer be just a walking corpse driven by revenge who cannot imagine a future. Only now can he truly live as himself.

In their heart lies a boiling passion, gripping the treasured sword, rehearsing the moment of drawing it countless times in their mind. The Ye is not actually their family surname. In order to uphold a promise that may never come to fruition, their family abandoned their own surname. The characters Yun in Ye Yun were chosen to commemorate the master their great‑grandfather served, Yue Yun. As the third‑generation male descendant of the Ye family, their life was arranged even before birth: to be a vessel, to serve the country loyally, and to die in that service. The world claims that Diancang Ye Yunzhao is a prodigy with the sword, but they themselves deeply disagree. Is there really such a thing as a genius in this world? It is the result of relentless practice day and night, painstakingly honed through dedication.

Even with unparalleled skills, he always approached life and people with utmost diligence, never becoming arrogant or complacent. He rarely engaged in fights with others; the moment Cloud Leaf Sword unsheathed, all who faced it met their demise without exception. Since descending the mountain to wander, there had never been an exception to this rule. Despite this, fearless individuals continued to flock and die one after another. Perhaps because of his sister's presence on this journey, he was particularly cautious, avoiding even his fellow sect brothers and masters. His superb martial arts, calm mind, cautious personality, and handsome appearance made Ye Yunzhao a legendary swordsman. Various titles began to be imposed upon him without considering how they might affect him, but personally, he preferred the title Cangsong Jianke. Before meeting you, his impression of the Tang Clan was not favorable.

The first swift swordsman of the Diancang Sect, they are one of the most renowned young heroes in the current Wulin. Their title comes from the admiration of the world, praising them for their strong character, as resilient and powerful as the pine and cypress, standing tall against the wind without wavering. Their swordsmanship talent is exceptional; since joining the Diancang Mountain at a young age, they have, in just a few short years, perused all seventeen sword manuals housed in the Songyun Pavilion of Diancang Mountain. Not to mention their peers, even their master laments being inferior.

A young swordsman dressed in Diancang sect attire. The name seems familiar, but you can't recall where you've heard it. For some reason, they are hiding their face beneath a bamboo hat. Judging by their handsome features, they don't seem like a bandit.

One of the most talked‑about legends in the Wulin among Jianghu practitioners. Among his many legendary exploits, his final showdown with the Supreme Bliss Sect Master was the most notable. Following the annihilation of the old Demon Sect, the strongest virtuous and evil experts disappeared without a trace, bringing an end to an era.

In the Tang Clan, everyone with the surname Tang is family. But you don't have the surname Tang, yet you are so familiar and close. I don't know how to categorize you. Mercurial Bell became extremely attentive towards you. She constantly sought to get closer, quietly staying near you. Her innocent eyes couldn't discern superficial beauty or ugliness; she simply greedily longed for a sense of security. She was not particularly concerned with Jianghu matters and couldn't even recognize the way down the mountain, yet she clearly admired you. The emotionless girl blossomed like a flower by your side, every ordinary day spent together being unparalleled.

Before the Sect Master's wife passed away, she had deceived their daughter by saying, I will retreat to Tang Clan's Secluded Valley for ten years of seclusion. If you miss me, fold a paper crane and send it down to the bottom of the valley. I will see it and know that you are thinking of your mother. Therefore, the Little Junior Sister folded paper cranes by her window every night for ten years, filled with thoughts of her mother. She feared the world, fearing that those she knew would leave one after another, and was terrified every night to the point of being unable to control herself.

Although she continued to practice kung fu, she did not particularly like it. At first, she often cried during the training. Practicing kung fu was extremely arduous, and she was also afraid of her father's punishment. Whenever she felt sad, she would run to her mother's embrace or seek refuge with the senior brother and second senior brother. After her mother passed away, she no longer ran away. Without realizing it, she had already mastered a set of punches and could finish her practice without sweating a single drop. She even forgot how to cry. She locked her emotions deep in her heart, keeping her true self hidden from everyone.

The Tang Clan's sole beloved daughter. The Sect Master was concerned about her delicate and frail body, so he sequestered himself in meditation for three years, developing a unique martial art based on a singular technique. He created the 'Heaven and Earth Unsound Formation' for his beloved daughter. Practitioners must tie seven sets of bells around their bodies; they must train diligently until they can run, leap, and throw hidden weapons without producing any sound. Only then will the task be considered complete. Influenced by this secret technique, she has a nature that is indifferent and rarely shows emotions. She does not enjoy speaking or making idle conversation. Her interest lies in paper folding.

Fragrant name Moling, Sect Master's only beloved daughter, a maiden like a forest creature. Her disposition is distant and indifferent, with seven silent bell‑pendants that never jingle. Her interest lies in paper folding.

He saved his affectionate senior sister from her forlorn love many years ago, but could not redeem her tears. The great mistake was already made, and the parties involved would never be able to let it go for the rest of their lives. Despite this, he still asked for his senior sister's hand in marriage, promising her a lifetime together. After several years of matrimony, they had a cherished child, but his beloved wife remained silent and melancholy throughout. Even though he could thrive in the Jianghu, it was difficult for him to bring peace to his home. Eventually, his wife succumbed to depression by leaping from a cliff, and Tang Zhongling's illness grew more severe.

He had led his disciples in a major battle to exterminate the old Demon Sect. He fought together with the Abbot of Songshan Temple against the Seven Immortals of Supreme Bliss Sect and broke through their Ten‑thousand Immortals Array, thwarting the ambitions of the Supreme Bliss Sect leader to dominate Central Plains. In the peak confrontation, Ren was one of the five representatives of the righteous faction, fighting against the Right Dharma Protector of Supreme Bliss Sect. He ingested a toxic drug to forcefully enhance his power and ultimately won this desperate battle against such a great evil, but in doing so, he left behind an incurable illness. After this battle, both Tang Clan and Songshan were severely weakened; however, Songshan was still revered by the people, while Tang Clan became an outcast that everyone despised.

The twenty‑seventh generation leader of the Tang Clan was known for their fiery temperament and deep‑seated hatred for evil in their youth. They roamed the Jianghu, using their unique ultimate technique, Flying Swallow Meteor Feather, to defeat all challengers. The reputation of the Tang Clan spread far and wide, but it also earned them many enemies among the heroes of the Jianghu. It was only after marrying a junior sister from the same clan and assuming the leadership that they began to adopt a more reserved demeanor. After managing the clan's affairs for over a decade, they have aged considerably. In recent years, due to stress‑related illness, they have entrusted the mundane tasks to their third disciple to handle on their behalf.

True name Tang Zhongling, he is the current head of the Tang Clan. With a fierce temper and a hatred for evil, he was once one of the legendary figures listed among the Ten Greatest Swordsmen of the Wulin. Unfortunately, after middle age, his physical condition had significantly declined, making Flying Swallow Meteor Feather his final masterpiece.

Fourth Senior Brother learned about his origins and discovered that his parents were alive. He had nine brothers and sisters who grew up in a well‑fed environment. This knowledge brought both envy and resentment, yet the heavy stone on his heart finally lifted. For years of accumulated grievances, seeing his blood‑related parents made him unable to express them. The exact reasons eluded him, and he felt these people were not ones to whine to. Ultimately, he politely declined his biological parents' invitation and returned to Tang Clan. Instead of enjoying the fine food, he still pestered his fellow disciples for plain meals. He was just as cunning and greedy as before, remaining obedient to the leader. Fourth Senior Brother also had his own family within Tang Clan.

Though Fourth Senior Brother made a fortune from dubious dealings, he also helped many in need. He sold magical swords and elixirs to warriors about to face death; secret manuals to youths avenging blood feuds; and carried letters across thousands of miles for those who wished to send them home. As long as the deal was struck, he would do his best to see it through. Although he coveted wealth, he did not look down on the poor or consider helping them a foolish investment. He was willing to assist, assuming that everyone had a long life ahead of them. He took on arduous mercantile missions no one else wanted in order to meet more people, establish his reputation, and find kin who might already be gone.

Often traveling south and north, he worked as a peddler. Though young in years, his experiences in the Jianghu were remarkably rich; he was well‑informed and had extensive connections. He could be found almost anywhere and sell anything. He had a not‑so‑flattering nickname: Without Holes, No Entry. He would always appear unexpectedly at critical moments where he was least expected, selling the goods you needed, which was extremely suspicious.

The closed‑door disciple of the Tang Clan's leader. Their background is unclear; they were discovered in a box of fruits while being brought up the mountain, and even as an infant, they had a remarkable appetite. On the surface, they are obedient and uphold honesty, particularly skilled at playing the innocent, earning the leader's trust and being entrusted with important financial responsibilities. They often take advantage of trips to purchase daily necessities like firewood, rice, oil, and salt to acquire various rare items, reselling them at high prices to the disciples within the clan for personal profit. If you can afford it, they will naturally be happy to help you smuggle in contraband.

Their real name is Weiyuan, a closed‑door disciple of the Tang Clan's leader. They have been entrusted with the task of going down the mountain to sell medicine and purchase daily necessities, which they enjoy immensely. They often exploit loopholes in the clan's rules, smuggling goods to sell at inflated prices to fellow disciples, earning a profit from the price difference.

He had once seen the emperor of the Great Song. I have strategies for stabilizing the nation and securing its borders, methods to nourish the people, plans to break through enemy lines‑only by purifying the palace can such things be achieved. He dared to offer this advice during his imperial audience after passing the imperial exams, but it offended those in power who accompanied the emperor. As a result, he was wrongfully accused and imprisoned under a false charge. His hometown's elders, his wife, and children all died unjustly. In jail, he wept for tens of days; on the day he was escorted to the execution ground, he was rescued by Tang Zhongling and two young disciples. Listen carefully, fellow villagers and elders‑this man suffered imprisonment merely because he sought to ensure the safety of the common people. He is truly the greatest hero in the land! Remember this! Tang Zhongling said thusly, and those words stayed deeply embedded in his heart, still unforgettable to this day.

In that year, under the pavilion during a heavy rain, they met Tang Zhongling and had a delightful conversation about the affairs of the world. What a joy it was! One was a poor scholar, and the other a wandering person of Jianghu. One was learned, the other skilled in martial arts; despite their differing perspectives, they developed a mutual respect for each other. Even after joining the Tang Clan to learn martial arts, their relationship resembled that of old friends, often enjoying tea together while discussing the passage of time. The Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother grew up right under their nose; although they held high positions, they never dared to consider themselves as older brothers. Unfortunately, starting martial arts too late meant they were ultimately behind in competing with the heroes of the world. That said, they were not one to seek strength or engage in conflict; as Sun Tzu's Art of War states, the highest form of warfare is to outsmart the enemy. The true winner is the one who avoids fighting.

The third directly transmitted disciple of Tang Clan's Sect Master. In his youth, he was full of fervor, studying hard for over a decade in seclusion, vowing to gain official rank and fame, using his knowledge and experience to benefit the nation. Unfortunately, he incurred the wrath of nobles by offending them and failed the imperial examination, leading to his life being endangered. Fortunately, he had once shared an umbrella with Tang Zhongling under a pavilion when they were both waiting for the rain. In times of danger, Tang Zhongling saved him from certain death at the gates of hell. After this experience, all his hopes were shattered, and he gave up on serving the court. He joined the Tang Clan instead. His interest lay in storytelling, often recounting tales of the Jianghu world during idle moments, without minding life and death, thus being quite unburdened.

Single name Sheng, Third Directly Inherited Disciple of Tang Clan. Brought his arts to seek a master, thus he is older than the two senior brothers in age. Previously, he was an ambitious scholar, but due to offending the nobility, he fled from the Jianghu. His interests include storytelling, teaching talented individuals, and jestingly discussing world affairs.

He revered his master Tang Zhongling more than his birth father, whom he had bid farewell to in childhood. Compared to the Mud Cult, Tang Clan felt more like home. He had not forgotten his mission, but his heart was no longer there. He pretended allegiance to the Mud Cult while secretly protecting the Tang Clan. He sifted through ancient and modern texts to find solutions for the old grievances of the Sect Leader. He was envious of the special favor shown by the eldest senior brother to the Sect Leader. Though he spoke harshly, he spoiled his half‑sister, Little Junior Sister Mo Ling, who shared a mother with him.

His true identity was that of an undercover agent from the Mud Cult's Human Path. Sent by the Demon Sect, he had been initiated into the Tang Clan since childhood to respond to the needs of the Mud Cult. He gained the trust of the Sect Master and was taught the secret formula for 'pepper powder.' Originally, he was supposed to use this to control Tang Clan disciples and serve the Mud Cult, but due to the Sect Master discontinuing the practice of using pepper powder as a poison in cultivation exercises, his plans did not come to fruition.

The second disciple under the Tang Clan's patriarch. Skilled in the use of poison, his knowledge of poisons surpasses that of his teacher. He is a meticulous and solitary individual, strict with himself and others. Ordered by his master to oversee discipline, he is greatly feared by his fellow disciples. He rarely leaves the alchemy laboratory and seldom ventures into Jianghu. Thus, his reputation does not extend as far as his senior brother's. However, those who have clashed with him admit they tremble even without cause. He has an unusual obsession with pepper powder, not only enjoying it himself but also forcing others to partake in it.

With the single name Zheng, is the second disciple under the Tang Clan's Sect Leader. Skilled in the use of poisons, he excels particularly in the study of poison and drug techniques, surpassing his own master. He is meticulous in thought, solitary and deeply introspective, rarely venturing down the mountain. Thus, his reputation does not extend as far as that of his senior brother. He is known by others as the 'Spicy Young Lord' or the 'Sharp‑Handed Young Master,' and people respect him from afar, avoiding direct contact with him.

Seeming carefree and indifferent to worldly matters, his demeanor was actually deeply rebellious and stubborn. As a young boy, he had tried every possible means to escape the Tang Clan, fleeing back home. His parents were at a loss for what to do, so they finally revealed his true identity to him, guiding him to seek out his birth mother. At Flower Moon Tower, he saw his mother, who was suffering from syphilis and had lost her mental clarity. From others, he learned that his mother had exhausted all her savings and entrusted someone to adopt him, clearing his name and then sending him into the Tang Clan to learn. Her intention was not to let her beloved son suffer as she did, always at the mercy of others and treated with contempt. After that day, Tang Buyi underwent a transformation, vowing to support women across the land.

Frequenting the Flower Moon Tower, they scattered silver like flowing water, earning the playful title of Owner from the girls there, and even the madam was quite fond of them. Their reputation as a hero spread far and wide, but they were also notorious. People in the Jianghu feared this young hero, yet there was no official title to restrain them, so families kept their wives and daughters under strict watch, fearing that this person might steal their hearts. As for the Little Junior Sister, they treated her with the same affection as a biological younger sister, having no other thoughts.

The first disciple under the leader of the Tang Clan. One of the most renowned young heroes in the Wulin, they are free‑spirited, cheerful, and unconcerned with trivial matters. Having once heard of injustices, they descended the mountain to eliminate corrupt officials and opened granaries to aid the people, leaving without a trace once the matter was resolved. They also pursued the fame of a beautiful person, traveling thousands of miles to meet them, only to vanish without a word after a brief encounter, earning a reputation for fickleness. Coming and going like the wind, they are known in Jianghu as the Flying Hero. They scoff at the Tang Clan's practice of distinguishing between inner and outer disciples, often encouraging their fellow disciples with different surnames to slack off and play, and are quite skilled at provoking their master's anger.

Named Yi Bu Yi, he is the sect leader's foremost disciple. With a sharp and unbounded nature, he is known in the Jianghu as 'Flying Hero.' His skills with hidden weapons and qinggong have both reached the finest level in the contemporary world.
Important medical texts from the Song Dynasty recorded multiple illustrations of herbal plants.
Compendium of Materia Medica

This manuscript records a fragment of the 'Nine Transformations Great Wheel Method,' one of the Three Treasures of Supreme Bliss Sect. This volume is only the upper half and focuses on the Heart Method; the cultivation techniques are not entirely complete.
Nine Turns of the Fragmented Scroll

This book includes popular paper‑folding schemes from ancient to modern times, such as paper boxes, boats, frogs, cranes, fish, flowers, swords, and cloud‑ladders. The illustrations are detailed, and the instructions are clear. With this book, anyone can become a paper‑folding warrior.
Collection of Origami

The full title is Huangdi's Eighty‑One Difficulties Classic, a renowned medical work aimed at elucidating the doubts and key points of the Huangdi Neijing. Traditionally attributed to the famous physician Bian Que, it emphasizes the theories of Five Evils Interference and Ten Transformations, explaining the relationships of the five organs, discussing pulse theory, meridians, organs, and even acupuncture methods, profoundly influencing later generations of medicine.
Nanjing

The medical book compiled by the Hanlin Medical Officer under the decree of Emperor Taizong includes methods of diagnosis, prescriptions, diseases of the five organs, internal and external medicine, gynecology, pediatrics, dietary practices, elixirs, external treatments, acupuncture, and more. The original text consists of a hundred volumes, but what you have received is merely an outline, as Second Senior Brother believes that the omitted content is common knowledge that you should already know.
Taiping Shenghui Fang

Wei Ju carefully selected a collection of contemporary outstanding literary works in verse, excerpting one hundred Song Dynasty ci poems. Her curation was precise and balanced, akin to a mirror reflecting the words with clarity. Not all of these may be penned by renowned masters, but they are certainly masterpieces. This book is a hand‑copied edition by Wei Ju, with delicate handwriting that resembles flowers adorning a beautiful lady, as graceful as a phoenix's flight or a swan's wander, frustrated in its ambitions. Yet any literati would delight upon seeing this volume; it alone was given to you, a person from the Jianghu. She adhered to her vow but harbored a private desire, secretly including some of her own old works under an anonymous name.
Selected Lyrics of Song Ci

The ancestral medical book of the Tang Clan is the only one in the world that uses poison as medicine. It combines the teachings of the Miao region and Buddhism, observing that a bowl of water contains eighty‑four thousand insects, which represent poison. These poisons are also categorized into the five elements and six harmonies, corresponding to the five organs and six bowels. Too much leads to harm, too little results in illness, depletion causes weakness, and imbalance leads to madness. It is not that people are not harmed by the five poisons; rather, their toxic properties have yet to manifest. Only by using medicine to nurture them, allowing them to flow harmoniously, can one turn poison to their advantage, making it difficult for a hundred ailments to invade.
Tang Clan Pharmacopoeia

Written by Zhang Zhongjing, a physician of the Eastern Han dynasty, this is a classic of Han medicine. The original text was lost due to wars and battles, but this book was compiled from the Shang Huan Lun and the Jin Gu Yao Lue.
Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases

The Medical Classic written by the Medicine King Sun Simiao is a monumental work that encompasses both empirical and theoretical prescriptions. This book is based on the organ theory of the Huangdi Neijing, collecting medical theories, prescriptions, medicinal uses, and acupuncture techniques, totaling two hundred and thirty categories and five thousand three hundred prescriptions. The opening chapter, Great Physicians and Sincere Intent, discusses medical ethics and the compassion for the world, leaving a profound impact on future generations.
Essential Formulas for Emergency Treatment

Mud Cult's Heavenly Path Demon Sect Heart Method. A cultivation qi gong evolved from medical texts, based on the traditional Chinese medicine 'warming method.' It uses warming and pungent drugs for moxibustion at acupoints to dispel cold qi, while also tonifying qi and nourishing blood‑extremely effective with the ability to restore yang and counteract yin.
Warm Yang Blood Circulation Talisman

A very new book, after many twists and turns, has finally made its way into your hands. The first half contains the famous phrases and lines of modern poets, including the masterpieces of Yan Shu, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, Liu Yong, and the three Su brothers. The latter half features the works of contemporary literati, but the last few pages have been deliberately defaced and are unreadable, with only the surname of the author, Wei, faintly visible.
Selection of Contemporary Poetry

Not only does the book cover the various weapons and tools of the Fire Flame Mountain Sword Pavilion, including their ironware blueprints, but it also encompasses undisclosed forging secrets. It records the characteristics, formulas, and properties of different metals and alloys. The book details processes such as annealing, quenching, and tempering utilizing the geothermal heat from Fire Flame Mountain, which is more authentic and rigorous compared to the forging techniques you are familiar with in the Tang Clan.
Fire Flame Mountain Forging Manual

Nangong Gaozu, hand‑copied manuscript by Alliance Leader Nangong Zhi of the Wulin Alliance. The handwriting is powerful, each stroke and dash seeming to sweep away thousands of soldiers, often used as a model for Nangong clan members to practice calligraphy. Although it does not record martial arts techniques, it includes various insights from Nangong Zhi's life such as military strategy, scholarship, medicine, heart journey, contemporary fashion trends, and jokes. In fact, this book is quite interesting to read.
Nangong Martial Preparedness Treatise

It records the forging methods of the secret weapons of the Four Gates of Kongtong, which contain many ingenious techniques and extraordinary craftsmanship. The mother‑and‑son mandarin duck axe, the mechanical saw, and the grappling hook with flying claws are all included. Even if you do not use these weapons, creating and studying them can certainly enhance your own skills.
Kongtong Xuanbing Forging Method

Renowned far and wide, the Nangong family martial arts school is not to be underestimated despite its graceful demeanor. The fan technique combines both offense and defense; the handle can strike acupoints, while the fan itself provides a deceptive counterattack. What appears as a feint becomes the real move, and those with strong internal energy can merely fan the air to harm an opponent. Once released, it spins freely, making it hard to guard against or evade. What makes them truly remarkable is their graceful bearing‑modest, unarrogant, and harmonious in demeanor.
Nangong Elegant Fan

When the Confucian war god Mencius roamed the various states, he engaged in debates with all comers using his lips as swords and tongues as spears, settling the central plain through his eloquent teachings. The origin of these sayings is uncertain, but in rural legends, the chess piece pao actually refers to Mencius's mouth, capable of killing from afar. The terrifying aspect lies in its precision; anyone can be targeted regardless of their status or respectful attitude during inquiries. Even when debating, he employed Sun Tzu's Art of War and neigong inner power, rendering one speechless under his scathing criticism, to the point that being literally verbally killed is not strange. He berated all the hundred schools of thought but forbade others from criticizing him; his anger was relentless: Am I fond of empty debate?! It is because I have no choice!! became a timeless masterpiece.
War God's Sayings

Jianghu Ghost Domain Record is an anonymous account written with his mouth instead of hands. The document describes how he went from a innocent and healthy child, tricked into poverty and ruin, wandering in a foreign land. Despite struggling to survive on his own, he was falsely accused of theft and sentenced to prison, where his arms were amputated. In the end, he managed to escape and took revenge by refining the peach seed spike inside the prison.
Jianghu Ghostly Chronicles: Continuation

A chronicle of various tricks and schemes in the Jianghu, the author's intent was to warn innocent civilians not to be deceived by others and to remember that one should not have thoughts of harming others but must always be wary. Unfortunately, this book fell into the wrong hands and was instantly transformed into a fraud manual, employing whatever means necessary to maximize its potency.
Jianghu Ghostly Chronicles

Notes written by Lei Qian, the current leader of the Kongtong Iron Fist Sect. Aware of their own limited talent, they fear that the skills of the previous generation may be lost. Although unable to create new paths, they have a grand ambition to compile various extraordinary techniques and methods into this book. This is a book written for mortals.
Miscellaneous Notes on Eighteen Unique Weapon Training Methods

Author Ye Yunshang's handwriting is very elegant and delicate, with a hint of juvenile fun, much like herself. This writing details her snowball fighting techniques, seriously dividing them into 'main attack' and 'sneak attack' sections. Most of the moves in this book are imagined by her. They include hiding stones or caterpillars in snowballs, stuffing snowballs into pants‑she leaves no stone unturned in her cruel tactics.
Snowball Combat Manual

Written by Sun Wu, the Spring and Autumn Military Saint, *The Art of War* is the earliest military treatise in Central Plains. Comprising thirteen chapters, it discusses military strategy and summarizes war experiences, profoundly influencing military tactics for generations to come.
Sun Tzu's Art of War

Composed from the sayings of Confucius, a prominent thinker of the Spring and Autumn period, this text is one of the most important classics in Confucianism. This simple vernacular version was compiled by Third Senior Brother when he served as a private school teacher to instruct children who could not read.
Analects

The mystical martial arts of the Qingcheng School blend the principles of Taiji, drawing qi into the bones to strengthen the spirit. In their palm, they cultivate all things; with each contraction and expansion, yin and yang, calm and movement are harmonized. Regardless of whether the opponent's force is yin or yang, it can be transformed and absorbed as if a clay ox entering the sea, dissipating without trace.
Yin and Yang Theft
Volume One of Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill
Volume One of Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill

Daoist Tiger Roar Technique is modeled after the fierce roar of a tiger, symbolizing the courage and perseverance of cultivators. It is said that practitioners who master this technique can emit a powerful and fearsome roar from their dantian, capable of frightening away evil forces as if they were fleeing before a charging tiger. When in combat, the user issues a roar like thunder, its sound echoing for miles, striking fear into the hearts of adversaries and potentially causing internal injuries.
Tiger Howl Skill

The Heart Method of Qingcheng's Neigong focuses on non‑action cultivation, maintaining emptiness to achieve voidness. A mind that is pure and inactive is actually active; achieving great perfection lies in having no thoughts or intentions. It is imperative not to dwell on any mental images or concepts, as the path arises naturally from this state. Though difficult to master, the day one attains true proficiency will be anything but trivial.
Wu Wei Dan Method

The heart method of the Shangguan family's three great aristocratic clans, the essence of the surging saber technique. It requires training with turbulent currents to hone one's skills, achieving the ability to stand firm in raging waves and slash through them. The techniques flow like the endless tide, pressing forward relentlessly, amplifying inner strength even further. Even if one manages to block them, they would stagger a few steps.
Wave Riding Technique

The legendary former Wulin Alliance Leader Long Yuan's famous skill was actually not a single martial art but seven distinct techniques that Long Yuan had mastered. These included both knives and swords: Slash through the Stellar Net; Punch and Claw: Mountain‑Cleaving Palm; Leg Techniques: Sun‑Cannon Kicks; Spear and Staff: Spear of the Tyrannical King; Long Rope: Strange Acupoint Rope; Hidden Weapon: Mindful Finger; Neigong: Xuan Xuan's Cultivation Art of Profound Creation. Many years ago, Long Yuan commanded the heroes and gathered them to invade the Demon Sect's old main temple. He single‑handedly fought against Joyful Eternity's Lord, Zhan Xing She Ri, using Bawang Ge Shan repeatedly, which greatly astonished the experts of both the righteous and villainous factions. Without prior agreement, they all secretly wished: This is indeed the greatest under heaven today.
Long Yuan Seven Absolutes

The Nangong family's generational legacy of the Heart Method is passed down, with each person receiving a copy, and the verses elegantly transcribed on the inner pages of the book. It blends Daoist philosophy, emphasizing that amidst countless changes, one remains steadfast; tranquility of spirit leads to calmness of mind, guarding the mysterious gateway, subduing malevolent energies, maintaining humility, and achieving clarity of heart and mind. The foundation of the Nangong family's teachings lies in safeguarding the heart, followed by protecting oneself, preserving the family, and defending the nation.
Nangong Heart Method

The leader of Jinxiang Palace, Fei Sha, painstakingly created this technique, which evolved from the Nangong Heart Method. Its purpose is to help individuals achieve a calm mind, preventing them from harming themselves due to sorrow. The term Xuan Zhu refers to the moon, and thus this practice is also known as the Moon Gazing Heart Sutra. People experience joy and sorrow, separation and reunion, just as the moon has its phases of brightness and darkness; this has always been difficult to attain in full. Yet, even when separated by distance, the same moonlight shines upon all. Whenever one feels overwhelmed with grief, they should practice this technique, gather their spirit, and transform sorrow into strength, living life to the fullest.
Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra

The Heart Method of the now non‑existent Snow Mountain Sect is practiced with very special methods. One must first inhale true qi deeply, then strip naked and insert their body upside down into the snow, only exposing their feet. Someone else would then apply moxibustion to the Yongquan acupoint on their soles, using the heat from the moxa to activate the meridians and adjust their body temperature to resist the cold and ice. If there is no snow water available, a nearby cool stream can be used as a substitute.
Snow Mountain Heart Method

The Flying Sky Sect and the Soul Stealer Sect are competing for the facade of Kongtong Sect. In their pursuit of rapid success, they spare no effort, even resorting to drinking poison to quench their thirst, using Scorpion Poison to enhance their internal strength and forcefully break through their bottleneck. By employing the Burning Heart Fire Seal, they can temporarily accelerate their heartbeat, promote blood flow, and enhance their physical abilities at the cost of burning their remaining lifespan. However, the price is not just this; the fire poison accumulates within the body, and when it reaches its peak, it manifests outwardly. Mild symptoms include dry mouth, bleeding gums, insomnia, and irritability, while severe cases can lead to a surge of heat in the head, resulting in either madness or sudden death. The danger is particularly pronounced during the Dragon Boat Festival when the yang energy is at its strongest, so caution is essential.
Heartburn Seal

The practitioner needs to stand on one foot and support the lute with their leg, which is the Qinggong technique of Flying Heaven Sect's Crane Pile. To pluck the Iron Zither's strings, they must first master Soul Stealer Sect's Frost Blade Piercing Bamboo Fingers; then to resonate the sound box, they need to use Mystic Skill Sect's Inner Power. When attacking an enemy, they can pick up the lute as a weapon and perform the Iron Fist Strange Art's As‑Wished Smash, smashing the enemy's head open. Upon completion of the cultivation, a single thought sets off a symphony in the hundred pulses, moving like the sound of a plucked string, enduring without decay; this is Kongtong's first divine technique.
Iron Pipa Skill

Hidden within the stalactite cave where the Wu Mountain meets the Yangtze River, mysterious martial arts techniques depicted on the walls in a series of nine connected drawings remain unknown regarding their origin or duration. Despite their seemingly balanced yet sinister nature, they are not ordinary training methods. Nevertheless, these images are concise and have a startling impact. A fisherman who accidentally fell into the water discovered them and copied them, presenting them to the Imperial Court for a reward. However, the court paid little attention, and this martial arts technique was subsequently buried among the shelves of officials and nobles. Additionally, due to rising water levels, the cave has been completely flooded.
Wushan Cave Mansion Nine Treasures Diagram

Although the effects are powerful and widely known, no one wishes to practice this qigong. This is because it is a technique for boys, which is quite regrettable. It is said that once a man marries, the hard‑earned power from practicing will dissipate. No one wants to end their days alone, so few are willing to cultivate this martial arts skill. However, this is a misunderstanding. The term boy's qigong refers to preserving the primordial energy to nourish the body's vitality since childhood. Thus, it is most effective when started from a young age. If one begins practicing immediately after birth, they can achieve great success within twelve years. Starting at the age of adolescence will reduce the effectiveness because the muscles and bones are already formed, and the primordial energy has dispersed. After reaching the age of thirty, there is no point in learning it at all. It has nothing to do with whether one marries or not.
Primordial Youth Qi

Daoist Azure Dragon's Sigh is likened to the Nine Heavens Dragon's Roar, describing a cultivator ascending to transcendence with a clear and resounding exhalation, akin to a dragon's cry piercing through the air. This cultivation technique requires the internal qi from the dantian to be externally emitted. When engaging in combat, one releases this power with a fierce howl, the sound like thunderbolts cascading for miles, capturing the opponent's soul and even causing internal injuries.
Dragon's Roar Technique

The military training exercises of the Yang family from the Northern Song Dynasty, known for their loyalty and bravery, are referred to as gymnastics. However, in order to truly enhance survival rates on the battlefield, the intensity of this training far exceeds that of the Imperial Court's regular army and is even stricter than the techniques of smaller sects in the Wulin. It incorporates staff techniques, the One Hundred and Eight Formation drills, and the Eighteen Strikes with the bronze hammer. This set of exercises would be challenging for even those from the Wulin to endure.
Yang Family Military Drill Manual

This mysterious meditation skill passed down from Tantric Buddhism of the Western Regions has a training method vastly different from that of Central Plain martial arts. Not only are its postures peculiar, but the language used is also extremely obscure. The final two chapters were translated poorly, making them difficult to read. Practicing this meditation requires physical effort; one must ignite charcoal and place sharp gravel beneath it, then practice on top of the stones. To prevent burning oneself, practitioners need to cultivate their neigong to expel heat from their bodies. It is said that those who reach the highest level can sit in meditation and float in mid‑air, extend their limbs to strike opponents, and even breathe out flames. However, without access to the final two chapters, it is impossible to know if this ultimate realm can actually be achieved.
Fiery Zen

To promote their doctrines and enlighten the common people, the Quanzhen Sect intentionally spread external neigong. They simplified the sword techniques, interspersing them with methods for nurturing life, rewriting them in simple spoken language to make them easy to understand. This allowed beginners to glimpse into Daoist studies, potentially extending one's lifespan. Every villager, including elders and children, could practice these exercises, making them akin to a national health routine. However, relying on this to defeat enemies or gain the upper hand would likely be ineffective.
Quanzhen Sword Technique

Beggar Sect's everyone knows a song called Lianhualuopei. It actually is a neigong dharma that teaches survival skills. After work every night, the more senior beggars lead the younger ones in singing it together. As they sing, they tap bowls with chopsticks to keep time, helping them coordinate their breathing with the song, thereby naturally cultivating breathing habits. However, the lyrics are often coarse and indecent, offending good manners. In some cases, singing them in front of a girl's family could even lead to an official complaint.
Lotus Falls

Classic tricks in the Jianghu often involve many small people. When enemies are too strong and one cannot match them, they seize an opportunity to seal off their meridians by regulating their internal energy, causing the lifeforce to stagnate and making their pulse temporarily stop, giving the appearance of death. Once the enemy departs, they can be revived using pre‑hidden lime in their palms which heats up upon contact with water. However, this neigong technique carries significant risks; if the mechanism fails to work properly when reviving, one might suffer from brain hypoxia and become mentally impaired for life. Moreover, should a ruthless figure appear and see them fallen, they would likely deliver two fatal blows without hesitation, turning fake death into real death.
Turtle Breathing Technique

The female hero of the Tang Clan, Tang Fen, based her unique martial arts on the Five Elements theory of the Eight Immortals Sword Technique from Qingcheng, substituting the elements with the Five Poisons. While the techniques may be considered at most second‑rate, they contain the intricate knowledge of both medicine and poison from the Tang Clan, making them quite difficult to comprehend. Even after studying them, one may not necessarily achieve significant success.
Eight Immortals Finger

Soul Stealer Iron Fist and Injury Fist from Mystic Skill Iron Guqin Technique are all derived from the lost divine arts mentioned in the Southern Peak True Scripture. The Flying Heaven Kick and the original Crane Shadow Footsteps form the foundation. When one masters this technique, they can stand on a single toe without bending their knee, relying solely on inner strength to glide at great speed. Upon releasing the foot, power flows from body through leg to toe, concentrating immense force into a pinpoint strike. Depending on intent, it can be used with either fierce or gentle force; it can pierce through the Golden Bell Robe with one toe, or block an opponent's acupoint with subtle pressure.
Barefoot Divine Skill

The extremely insane Blade Technique was created by a third‑rate Blade Master burdened with the hatred of having their spouse taken away. During the 13 years of wrongful imprisonment, they contemplated the enemy's martial arts paths thousands of times in their heart, imagining torturing the rival who took their spouse away tens of thousands of times in their mind. Shortly after their release from prison, the shocking bloodshed case known as 'Crimson Blood Massacre' erupted, stirring the Jianghu.
A thousand blades and ten thousand cuts to kill.

Your revered mentor Xiahou Lan gathered the essence of the Soul Stealer and the divine core of two snowy mountain families. After refining and blending it with the Controlling Crane Qi Gong, she finally created this divine technique. Its purpose is not to kill or wound but specifically for countering skilled opponents. Even the highest level of Qinggong can be caught by it.  The force is delivered precisely as if a flying goose were stepping on snow, leaving behind only occasional prints. The geese have long since flown away, east or west does it matter? It lightly and subtly grabs, using three parts of power while hiding seven parts. The follow‑up attack remains concealed. By disrupting the enemy's stance, I swiftly replenish my energy to launch a deadly assault.
Snow Mountain Flying Swan Claw

The martial art technique known as Treading the Moon, created by your Tang Clan senior brother Dengtuzi due to his licentious behavior and recorded in The Sequel to Ascending Cloud Ladder, is one of the offensive moves derived from this path of qinggong. In order to see a beauty, one can ascend the tower using the Ascending Cloud Ladder. The Treading the Moon move specifically refers to stepping on opponents' weapons, taking advantage of your elevated position to step down and crush their faces. Moon here symbolizes light or brilliance, hinting at all blades or weapons that are directed towards oneself. Therefore, the true meaning of Treading the Moon is to step directly onto others' weapons from a high vantage point and stomp on their face.
Dengyun Ta, Wangyue

The Soul Stealer's signature technique in the Jianghu.
